verses.1:1: And it happened that after Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian, who first reigned in Greece, having gone out from the land of Kittim, struck Darius, king of the Persians and Medes,
verses.1:2: he waged many battles, and captured the fortifications of all, and killed the kings of the earth,
verses.1:3: and he passed through as far as the ends of the earth, and took the spoils of a multitude of nations, and the earth fell silent in his sight.
verses.1:4: And he gathered a force and an exceedingly strong army, and his heart was exalted and lifted up.
verses.1:5: And after these things he fell upon his bed, and knew that he was dying.
verses.1:6: And he called his noble servants, who had been brought up with him from youth, and divided his kingdom among them while he was still living.
verses.1:7: And Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
verses.1:8: And his servants obtained the kingdom, each one in his own place,
verses.1:9: and they all placed diadems on themselves after his death, and their sons after them for many years, and evils were multiplied on the earth.
verses.1:10: And a sinful root came out from them, Antiochus the Illustrious, son of Antiochus the king, who had been a hostage in Rome; and he reigned in the one hundred thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
verses.1:11: In those days, wicked sons came out from Israel and persuaded many, saying, "Let us go and establish a covenant with the nations that are around us, because since we departed from them, many evils have found us."
verses.1:12: And the saying appeared good in their eyes.
verses.1:13: And some of the people were determined, and they went to the king, and he gave them authority to practice the ordinance of the nations.
verses.1:14: And they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the laws of the nations,
verses.1:15: and they made foreskins for themselves, and departed from the holy covenant, and were joined to the nations, and were sold to do evil.
verses.1:16: And the kingdom was made ready in the sight of Antiochus, and he began to reign in the land of Egypt so that he might reign over two kingdoms.
verses.1:17: And he entered into Egypt with a massive multitude, with chariots, and elephants, and horsemen, and a vast multitude of ships,
verses.1:18: and he waged war against Ptolemy, king of Egypt; and Ptolemy was afraid before his face, and fled, and many fell wounded.
verses.1:19: And he seized the fortified cities in the land of Egypt, and took the spoils of the land of Egypt.
verses.1:20: And Antiochus turned back after he struck Egypt in the one hundred forty-third year, and he went up to Israel.
verses.1:21: And he entered into the sanctuary with arrogance, and took the golden altar, and the lampstand of light, and all its vessels, and the table of presentation, and the libation cups, and the bowls, and the small golden mortars, and the veil, and the crowns, and the golden ornament that was on the front of the temple; and he shattered everything.
verses.1:22: And he went up to Jerusalem with a massive multitude.
verses.1:23: And he took the silver, and the gold, and the desirable vessels, and he took the hidden treasures that he found; and having carried everything off, he departed into his own land.
verses.1:24: And he carried out a slaughter of people, and spoke in great arrogance.
verses.1:25: And great mourning arose in Israel, and in every place of theirs,
verses.1:26: and the rulers and elders groaned; virgins and young men grew weak, and the beauty of the women was altered.
verses.1:27: Every husband took up a lament, and those who sat on the marriage bed were grieving,
verses.1:28: and the land was shaken over those dwelling in it, and the entire house of Jacob put on shame.
verses.1:29: And after two years of days, the king sent the chief of tributes into the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a great crowd.
verses.1:30: And he spoke peaceful words to them in deceit, and they believed him.
verses.1:31: And he took the spoils of the city, and burned it with fire, and destroyed its houses and its walls all around,
verses.1:32: and they led the women away as captives, and took possession of the children and the livestock.
verses.1:33: And they built up the city of David with a great and strong wall and strong towers, and it became a citadel for them,
verses.1:34: and they placed there a sinful nation, wicked men, and they grew strong in it; and they laid up weapons and food, and gathered the spoils of Jerusalem,
verses.1:35: and stored them there; and they became a great snare.
verses.1:36: And this became an ambush against the sanctuary, and an evil adversary in Israel,
verses.1:37: and they shed innocent blood all around the sanctuary, and they polluted the sanctuary.
verses.1:38: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and she became a dwelling of strangers, and she became a stranger to her own offspring, and her children abandoned her.
verses.1:39: Her sanctuary was made desolate like a wilderness; her feast days were turned into mourning, her Sabbaths into reproach, her honors into nothing.
verses.1:40: According to her glory her dishonor was multiplied, and her loftiness was turned into mourning.
verses.1:41: And King Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom that all the people should be one, and that each one should abandon his own law.
verses.1:42: And all the nations agreed according to the word of King Antiochus,
verses.1:43: and many from Israel agreed to his service, and sacrificed to idols, and defiled the Sabbath.
verses.1:44: And the king sent letters through the hands of messengers into Jerusalem and into all the cities of Judah, that they should follow the laws of the nations of the land,
verses.1:45: and prohibit burnt offerings and sacrifices and propitiations from being made in the temple of God;
verses.1:46: and he commanded the holy things and the holy people of Israel to be defiled.
verses.1:47: And he commanded altars and temples and idols to be built, and the flesh of swine and profane livestock to be offered in sacrifice,
verses.1:48: and to leave their sons uncircumcised, and their souls to be defiled with all unclean things and abominations, so that they would forget the law and alter all the ordinances of God,
verses.1:50: and that whoever did not act according to the word of King Antiochus should die.
verses.1:51: According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom, and he appointed rulers over the people who would compel these things to be done.
verses.1:52: And many from the people gathered to those who had abandoned the law of the Lord, and they did evils on the earth;
verses.1:53: and they drove the people of Israel into hidden places and into secret places of fugitives.
verses.1:54: On the fifteenth day of the month of Chislev, in the one hundred forty-fifth year, King Antiochus built an abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God, and throughout all the cities of Judah all around they built altars;
verses.1:55: and before the doors of the houses and in the streets they were burning incense and sacrificing;
verses.1:56: and they burned the books of the law of God with fire, tearing them apart;
verses.1:57: and with whomever the books of the covenant of the Lord were found, and whoever observed the law of the Lord, according to the edict of the king they slaughtered him.
verses.1:58: In their power they were doing these things to the people of Israel who were found in each and every month in the cities.
verses.1:59: And on the twenty-fifth day of the month they were sacrificing upon the altar that was opposite the altar.
verses.1:60: And the women who circumcised their sons were slaughtered according to the command of King Antiochus,
verses.1:61: and they hanged the boys by the necks throughout all their houses, and they slaughtered those who had circumcised them.
verses.1:62: And many from the people of Israel resolved within themselves that they would not eat unclean things, and they chose to die rather than to be defiled by unclean foods;
verses.1:63: and they were unwilling to break the holy law of God, and they were slaughtered;
verses.1:64: and very great wrath came upon the people.
verses.2:1: In those days Mattathias, son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled on Mount Modin.
verses.2:2: And he had five sons: John, who bore the surname Gaddi;
verses.2:3: and Simon, who bore the surname Thassi;
verses.2:4: and Judas, who was called Maccabeus;
verses.2:5: and Eleazar, who bore the surname Avaran; and Jonathan, who bore the surname Apphus.
verses.2:6: These men saw the evils that were being done among the people of Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.2:7: And Mattathias said, "Woe to me! Why was I born to see the ruin of my people and the ruin of the holy city, and to sit there while she is given into the hands of enemies?
verses.2:8: The holy places have come into the hand of foreigners; her temple is like a man without honor.
verses.2:9: The vessels of her glory have been carried away captive; her old men have been slaughtered in the streets, and her young men have fallen by the sword of enemies.
verses.2:10: What nation has not inherited her kingdom and has not obtained her spoils?
verses.2:11: All her adornment has been taken away. She who was free has become a slave woman.
verses.2:12: And look, our holy places, and our beauty, and our splendor have been laid waste, and the nations have defiled them.
verses.2:13: Why, therefore, should we live any longer?"
verses.2:14: And Mattathias and his sons tore their clothes, and covered themselves with sackcloth, and mourned deeply.
verses.2:15: And those who had been sent by King Antiochus came there to force those who had fled into the city of Modin to offer sacrifice, and to burn incense, and to depart from the law of God.
verses.2:16: And many of the people of Israel, consenting, came forward to them, but Mattathias and his sons stood firm.
verses.2:17: And those who had been sent by Antiochus answered and said to Mattathias, "You are a leader, both most distinguished and great in this city, and adorned with sons and brothers.
verses.2:18: Therefore, come forward first and carry out the king's decree, just as all the nations have done, and the men of Judah, and those who remained in Jerusalem; and you and your sons will be among the friends of the king, and enriched with gold and silver and many gifts."
verses.2:19: And Mattathias answered and said with a loud voice, "Even if all the nations obey King Antiochus, so that each one departs from the service of the law of his fathers and consents to his commands,
verses.2:20: I and my sons and my brothers will obey the law of our fathers.
verses.2:21: May God be gracious to us; it is not beneficial for us to abandon the law and the ordinances of God.
verses.2:22: We will not listen to the words of King Antiochus, nor will we sacrifice, transgressing the commands of our law to go by another way."
verses.2:23: And when he stopped speaking these words, a certain Jew came forward in the sight of all to sacrifice to idols on the altar in the city of Modin, according to the king's decree.
verses.2:24: And Mattathias saw it and was grieved, and his inward parts trembled, and his fury was kindled according to the judgment of the law; and leaping forward, he slaughtered him on the altar.
verses.2:25: And at that very time he also killed the man whom King Antiochus had sent, who was forcing them to offer sacrifice, and he destroyed the altar.
verses.2:26: And he was zealous for the law, just as Phinehas did to Zimri, son of Salomi.
verses.2:27: And Mattathias cried out with a loud voice in the city, saying, "Everyone who has zeal for the law, upholding the covenant, let him come out after me."
verses.2:28: And he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left behind whatever they had in the city.
verses.2:29: Then many who were seeking justice and righteousness went down into the desert,
verses.2:30: and they settled there, they themselves and their sons and their wives and their livestock, because evils had flooded over them.
verses.2:31: And it was reported to the king's men and to the army that was in Jerusalem, the city of David, that certain men who had broken the king's command had departed to hidden places in the desert, and that many had gone after them.
verses.2:32: And immediately they went to them and prepared battle against them on the Sabbath day.
verses.2:33: And they said to them, "Do you still resist even now? Come out, and do according to the word of King Antiochus, and you will live."
verses.2:34: And they said, "We will not come out, nor will we do the word of the king so as to profane the Sabbath day."
verses.2:35: And they launched battle against them.
verses.2:36: And they did not answer them, nor did they throw a stone at them, nor did they block up the hidden places,
verses.2:37: saying, "Let us all die in our innocence; and heaven and earth will be witnesses over us that you are destroying us unjustly."
verses.2:38: And they brought war upon them on the Sabbath; and they died, they themselves, and their wives, and their children, and their livestock, up to a thousand human lives.
verses.2:39: And Mattathias and his friends learned of it, and they grieved greatly over them.
verses.2:40: And each man said to his neighbor, "If we all do just as our brothers have done and do not fight against the nations for our lives and our statutes, now they will quickly destroy us from the earth."
verses.2:41: And they resolved on that day, saying, "Every man, whoever comes against us in war on the Sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we will not all die, as our brothers died in the hidden places."
verses.2:42: Then a company of Hasideans, mighty in strength from Israel, was gathered to them, everyone willingly devoted to the law;
verses.2:43: and all who were fleeing from the evils were added to them and became a support to them.
verses.2:44: And they gathered an army, and struck down sinners in their wrath and wicked men in their indignation; and the rest fled to the nations to escape.
verses.2:45: And Mattathias and his friends went around and destroyed the altars;
verses.2:46: and they circumcised the uncircumcised boys, as many as they found within the borders of Israel, even by force.
verses.2:47: And they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands;
verses.2:48: and they secured the law from the hands of the nations and from the hands of the kings, and they had not given a horn to the sinner.
verses.2:49: And the days drew near for Mattathias to die, and he said to his sons, "Now pride has grown strong, and chastisement, and a time of overthrow, and the wrath of indignation.
verses.2:50: Now therefore, sons, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers,
verses.2:51: and remember the works of the fathers, which they did in their generations; and you will receive great glory and an eternal name.
verses.2:52: Was not Abraham found faithful in testing, and it was counted to him as righteousness?
verses.2:53: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the command, and became lord of Egypt.
verses.2:54: Phinehas our father, by being zealous with the zeal of God, received the covenant of an eternal priesthood.
verses.2:55: Joshua, when he fulfilled the word, became a leader in Israel.
verses.2:56: Caleb, when he testified in the assembly, received an inheritance.
verses.2:57: David in his mercy obtained the throne of the kingdom forever.
verses.2:58: Elijah, while he was zealous with zeal for the law, was received into heaven.
verses.2:59: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, believing, were delivered from the flame.
verses.2:60: Daniel in his innocence was delivered from the mouth of lions.
verses.2:61: And so consider through generation after generation that all who hope in Him do not grow weak.
verses.2:62: And do not be afraid of the words of a sinful man, because his glory is dung and a worm;
verses.2:63: today he is exalted, and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth, and his thought has perished.
verses.2:64: You, therefore, sons, be strong and act courageously in the law, because in it you will be glorious.
verses.2:65: And look, Simon your brother, I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him always, and he will be a father to you.
verses.2:66: And Judas Maccabeus, mighty in strength from his youth, let him be commander of the army for you, and he himself will wage the war of the people.
verses.2:67: And you will bring to yourselves all the doers of the law, and execute the vengeance of your people.
verses.2:68: Repay retribution to the nations, and pay heed to the precept of the law."
verses.2:69: And he blessed them, and was joined to his fathers.
verses.2:70: And he died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year; and he was buried by his sons in the tombs of his fathers in Modin, and all Israel mourned him with great mourning.
verses.3:1: And his son Judas, who was called Maccabeus, arose in his place;
verses.3:2: and all his brothers and all who had joined themselves to his father helped him, and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness.
verses.3:3: And he extended glory for his people, and put on a breastplate like a giant, and strapped on his weapons of war in battles, and protected the camp with his sword.
verses.3:4: He became like a lion in his deeds, and like a lion cub roaring in the hunt.
verses.3:5: And he pursued the wicked, searching them out, and those who troubled his people he burned with flames;
verses.3:6: and his enemies were driven back because of fear of him, and all the workers of wickedness were troubled, and deliverance was directed in his hand.
verses.3:7: And he embittered many kings, and gladdened Jacob in his deeds, and his memory is in blessing forever.
verses.3:8: And he passed through the cities of Judah, and destroyed the ungodly out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.
verses.3:9: And he became renowned to the farthest end of the earth, and he gathered those who were perishing.
verses.3:10: And Apollonius gathered the nations, and from Samaria a numerous and great force, to wage war against Israel.
verses.3:11: And Judas learned of it and went out to meet him, and he struck and killed him; and many fell wounded, and the rest fled.
verses.3:12: And he took their spoils, and Judas took away the sword of Apollonius, and he fought with it all his days.
verses.3:13: And Seron, commander of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had gathered a congregation of the faithful and an assembly with him,
verses.3:14: and he said, "I will make a name for myself, and I will be glorified in the kingdom, and I will wage war against Judas and those who are with him, who despised the word of the king."
verses.3:15: And he prepared himself, and a force of the ungodly, strong helpers, went up with him to execute vengeance on the sons of Israel.
verses.3:16: And they drew near as far as Beth-horon, and Judas went out to meet him with a few men.
verses.3:17: But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas, "How will we, being few, be able to fight against a multitude so great and so strong, when we are weary from fasting today?"
verses.3:18: And Judas said, "It is easy for many to be shut up into the hands of a few, and there is no difference in the sight of the God of heaven in delivering by many or by a few;
verses.3:19: for victory in war is not in the multitude of an army, but strength is from heaven.
verses.3:20: They come against us with an insolent multitude and pride, to destroy us and our wives and our children, and to plunder us;
verses.3:21: but we will fight for our lives and our laws;
verses.3:22: and the Lord Himself will crush them before our face; as for you, do not fear them."
verses.3:23: Now when he stopped speaking, he sprang upon them suddenly, and Seron and his army were crushed in his sight;
verses.3:24: and he pursued him along the descent of Beth-horon as far as the plain, and eight hundred men from among them fell, but the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
verses.3:25: And the fear of Judas and of his brothers, and dread, fell upon all the nations around them;
verses.3:26: and his name reached the king, and all the nations were telling about the battles of Judas.
verses.3:27: Now when King Antiochus heard these words, he became angry in spirit, and he sent and gathered the army of his entire kingdom, a very strong force;
verses.3:28: and he opened his treasury and gave pay to the army for a year, and he commanded them to be ready for everything.
verses.3:29: And he saw that the money had failed from his treasuries, and that the tributes of the region were small because of the dissension and calamity that he had caused in the land in order to take away the ordinances which were from the first days;
verses.3:30: and he feared that he would not have enough, as he had once and twice, for the expenses and gifts that he had given before with a generous hand; and he had abounded beyond the kings who had been before him.
verses.3:31: And he was greatly dismayed in spirit, and he planned to go into Persia, and to collect the tributes of the regions, and to gather much silver.
verses.3:32: And he left Lysias, a noble man of royal lineage, over the royal affairs from the river Euphrates as far as the river of Egypt,
verses.3:33: and to raise his son Antiochus until he returned.
verses.3:34: And he handed over to him half the army and the elephants, and he commanded him concerning everything that he wanted, and concerning those inhabiting Judea and Jerusalem;
verses.3:35: and that he should send an army against them to crush and uproot the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to take away their memory from the place;
verses.3:36: and that he should settle foreign sons as inhabitants in all their borders, and distribute their land by lot.
verses.3:37: And the king took part of the remaining army, and went out from Antioch, the city of his kingdom, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year; and he crossed the river Euphrates and passed through the upper regions.
verses.3:38: And Lysias chose Ptolemy the son of Dorymenes, and Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men from among the friends of the king;
verses.3:39: and he sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand horsemen to come into the land of Judah and destroy it according to the word of the king.
verses.3:40: And they marched out with all their force, and they came and encamped at Emmaus in the plain country.
verses.3:41: And the merchants of the regions heard their name, and they took silver and very much gold and servants, and came into the camp to take the sons of Israel as slaves; and the armies of Syria and of the land of the foreigners were added to them.
verses.3:42: And Judas and his brothers saw that evils had multiplied and that armies were encamping at their borders, and they learned the words of the king, which he had commanded to be done to the people for destruction and utter end;
verses.3:43: and they said, each one to his neighbor, "Let us raise up the ruin of our people, and let us fight for our people and our holy places."
verses.3:44: And the assembly was gathered so that they might be ready for battle, and so that they might pray and ask for mercy and compassions.
verses.3:45: And Jerusalem was uninhabited, but was like a desert; there was no one of her children who went in and went out. And the holy place was trampled down, and the sons of foreigners were in the citadel; there was the dwelling place of the nations. And delight was taken away from Jacob, and the flute and harp ceased there.
verses.3:46: And they were gathered together and came to Mizpah, opposite Jerusalem, because there was a place of prayer in Mizpah formerly in Israel.
verses.3:47: And they fasted on that day, and put on sackcloth, and placed ashes on their heads, and tore their garments;
verses.3:48: and they spread out the books of the law, concerning which the nations searched the likeness of their idols;
verses.3:49: and they brought the priestly vestments, and the firstfruits, and the tithes, and they raised up the Nazirites who had completed the days,
verses.3:50: and they cried out with a loud voice to heaven, saying, "What will we do with these, and where will we lead them?
verses.3:51: And Your holy places have been trampled down and defiled, and Your priests have been brought into mourning and humiliation;
verses.3:52: and look, the nations have assembled against us to destroy us; You know what they are planning against us.
verses.3:53: How will we be able to stand before their face, unless You, God, help us?"
verses.3:54: And with trumpets they cried out with a loud voice.
verses.3:55: And after these things Judas appointed leaders of the people: tribunes, and centurions, and commanders of fifty, and decurions.
verses.3:56: And he said to those who were building houses, and betrothing wives, and planting vineyards, and to the fearful, that they should return, each one to his own house, according to the law.
verses.3:57: And they moved the camp and stationed it to the south of Emmaus.
verses.3:58: And Judas said, "Arm yourselves, and be mighty sons, and be ready in the morning to fight against these nations that have assembled against us to destroy us and our holy places;
verses.3:59: for it is better for us to die in war than to see the evils of our nation and of the holy places.
verses.3:60: But as the will in heaven may be, so let it be done."
verses.4:1: And Gorgias took five thousand men and one thousand chosen horsemen, and they moved camp by night,
verses.4:2: so that they might draw near to the camp of the Jews and strike them suddenly; and the sons who were from the citadel were guides for them.
verses.4:3: And Judas heard, and he himself and the mighty men rose up to strike the force of the king's armies that were in Emmaus,
verses.4:4: for the army was still scattered away from the camp.
verses.4:5: And Gorgias came into the camp of Judas by night and found no one; and he was searching for them in the mountains, because he said, "These men are fleeing from us."
verses.4:6: And when day had come, Judas appeared in the plain with only three thousand men, who did not have armor and swords;
verses.4:7: and they saw the strong camp of the nations, and men wearing breastplates and cavalry around them, and these were trained for battle.
verses.4:8: And Judas said to the men who were with him, "Do not fear their multitude, and do not dread their onslaught.
verses.4:9: Remember how our fathers were saved in the Red Sea when Pharaoh was pursuing them with a large army.
verses.4:10: And now let us cry out to heaven, and the Lord will have mercy on us, and will be mindful of the covenant of our fathers, and will crush this army before our face today,
verses.4:11: and all the nations will know that there is One who redeems and frees Israel."
verses.4:12: And the foreigners lifted up their eyes and saw them coming from the opposite direction.
verses.4:13: And they went out from the camp into battle, and those who were with Judas blew the trumpet.
verses.4:14: And they clashed, and the nations were crushed and fled into the plain.
verses.4:15: But all those in the rear fell by the sword; and they pursued them as far as Gezer, and as far as the plains of Idumea, and of Azotus, and of Jamnia, and up to three thousand men fell from among them.
verses.4:16: And Judas returned, and his army was following him.
verses.4:17: And he said to the people, "Do not covet the plunder, because war is against us,
verses.4:18: and Gorgias and his army are near us on the mountain; but stand now against our enemies and fight against them, and afterward you will take the plunder securely."
verses.4:19: And while Judas was still speaking these things, look, a certain division appeared gazing out from the mountain.
verses.4:20: And Gorgias saw that his own men had been turned to flight and that they had set fire to the camp; for the smoke that was seen made clear what had been done.
verses.4:21: When they caught sight of these things, they were greatly afraid, seeing at the same time both Judas and the army in the plain ready for battle.
verses.4:22: And they all fled into the plain of the foreigners,
verses.4:23: and Judas returned to the plunder of the camp, and they took much gold, and silver, and blue, and sea purple, and great wealth.
verses.4:24: And turning back, they were singing a hymn and blessing God toward heaven, for He is good, for His mercy is forever.
verses.4:25: And a great deliverance came about in Israel on that day.
verses.4:26: Now whoever of the foreigners escaped came and reported to Lysias all the things that had happened.
verses.4:27: When he heard these things, dismayed in spirit, he was losing heart, because such things did not happen in Israel as he wished and as the king commanded.
verses.4:28: And in the following year, Lysias gathered sixty thousand chosen men and five thousand horsemen, so that he might conquer them.
verses.4:29: And they came into Judea and pitched camp at Beth-horon, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
verses.4:30: And they saw the strong army, and he prayed and said, "Blessed are You, Savior of Israel, who crushed the onslaught of the mighty one by the hand of Your servant David, and handed over the camp of the foreigners into the hand of Jonathan the son of Saul and of his armor-bearer.
verses.4:31: Enclose this army in the hand of Your people Israel, and let them be put to shame in their army and horsemen.
verses.4:32: Give them terror, and melt away the boldness of their strength, and let them be shaken by their crushing.
verses.4:33: Cast them down by the sword of those who love You, and let all who know Your name praise You together in hymns."
verses.4:34: And they joined battle, and five thousand men fell from the army of Lysias.
verses.4:35: Now Lysias, seeing the flight of his own men and the boldness of the Jews, and that they were ready either to live or to die bravely, went away to Antioch and chose soldiers, so that, being multiplied, they might come again into Judea.
verses.4:36: Now Judas and his brothers said, "Look, our enemies are crushed; let us go up now to cleanse the holy places and renew them."
verses.4:37: And the whole army was gathered together, and they went up to Mount Zion.
verses.4:38: And they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned up, and in the courts shrubs grown up as in a forest or on the mountains, and the priests' chambers torn down.
verses.4:39: And they tore their garments, and lamented with a great lamentation, and put ashes on their heads,
verses.4:40: and fell on their faces on the ground, and sounded out with the signal trumpets, and cried out to heaven.
verses.4:41: Then Judas appointed men to fight against those who were in the citadel, until they cleansed the holy places.
verses.4:42: And he chose priests without blemish, having delight in the law of God;
verses.4:43: and they cleansed the holy places and carried the stones of defilement to an unclean place.
verses.4:44: And he deliberated concerning the altar of burnt offerings, which had been profaned, what he should do with it.
verses.4:45: And a good plan occurred to them, that they should tear it down, so that it might not perhaps be a reproach to them, because the nations had defiled it; and they demolished it.
verses.4:46: And they stored away the stones on the mountain of the house in a suitable place, until a prophet should come and answer concerning them.
verses.4:47: And they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar like the one that was before;
verses.4:48: and they built the holy places and the things that were within the interior of the house, and they sanctified both the shrine and the courts.
verses.4:49: And they made new holy vessels, and brought the lampstand, and the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.
verses.4:50: And they placed incense on the altar, and lit the lamps that were on the lampstand, and they shone in the temple.
verses.4:51: And they placed loaves on the table, and hung the curtains, and completed all the works that they had done.
verses.4:52: And they rose up before morning on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month (this is the month of Chislev) of the one hundred and forty-eighth year,
verses.4:53: and offered sacrifice according to the law on the new altar of burnt offerings that they had made.
verses.4:54: At the time and on the day on which the nations had defiled it, on that very day it was renewed with songs, and harps, and lyres, and with cymbals.
verses.4:55: And all the people fell on their faces, and worshiped, and toward heaven blessed Him who had given them success.
verses.4:56: And they kept the dedication of the altar for eight days, and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and a sacrifice of salvation and of praise.
verses.4:57: And they adorned the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, and dedicated the gates and the priests' chambers, and set doors on them.
verses.4:58: And there was very great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.
verses.4:59: And Judas, and his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel decreed that the day of the dedication of the altar should be observed in its seasons from year to year for eight days from the twenty-fifth day of the month of Chislev, with gladness and joy.
verses.4:60: And at that time they built up Mount Zion, and high walls and strong towers all around, so that the nations might never come and trample it down as they had done before.
verses.4:61: And he stationed an army there to guard it, and he fortified it to watch over Beth-zur, so that the people might have a stronghold facing Idumea.
verses.5:1: And it happened that when the nations all around heard that the altar and the sanctuary had been built as before, they became very angry,
verses.5:2: and they planned to destroy the descendants of Jacob who were among them, and they began to kill some of the people and to persecute them.
verses.5:3: And Judas waged war against the sons of Esau in Idumea and those who were in Acrabattene, because they were besieging the Israelites; and he struck them with a great blow.
verses.5:4: And he remembered the wickedness of the sons of Baean, who were a snare and a stumbling block to the people, lying in ambush for them along the road.
verses.5:5: And they were shut up by him in the towers, and he encamped against them, and devoted them to destruction, and burned their towers with fire, together with all who were in them.
verses.5:6: And he crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and found a strong force and a numerous people, and Timothy their leader;
verses.5:7: and he engaged in many battles with them, and they were crushed in their sight, and he struck them down;
verses.5:8: and he captured the city of Gazer and its daughters, and returned to Judea.
verses.5:9: And the nations that were in Gilead gathered together against the Israelites who were within their borders to destroy them; and they fled into the fortress of Dathema.
verses.5:10: And they sent letters to Judas and his brothers, saying, "The nations all around have gathered together against us to do away with us,
verses.5:11: and they are preparing to come and seize the fortress into which we have fled, and Timothy is the leader of their army.
verses.5:12: Now therefore, come and rescue us from their hands, because a multitude of us have fallen.
verses.5:13: And all our brothers who were in the districts of Tubin have been killed; and they have led away captive their wives and children, and the spoils, and have put to death about one thousand men there."
verses.5:14: And the letters were still being read, and look, other messengers came from Galilee with their tunics torn, reporting according to these words,
verses.5:15: saying that people had assembled against them from Ptolemais, Tyre, and Sidon: "And all Galilee has been filled with foreigners to wipe us out."
verses.5:16: Now when Judas and the people heard these words, a great assembly came together to consider what they should do for their brothers who were in distress and were being attacked by them.
verses.5:17: And Judas said to Simon his brother, "Choose men for yourself, and go and deliver your brothers in Galilee; but I and my brother Jonathan will go into Gilead."
verses.5:18: And he left Joseph the son of Zechariah, and Azariah, leaders of the people, with the rest of the army in Judea to keep guard;
verses.5:19: and he commanded them, saying, "Take charge of this people, and do not engage in battle against the nations until we return."
verses.5:20: And three thousand men were allotted to Simon to go into Galilee, and to Judas, eight thousand for Gilead.
verses.5:21: And Simon went into Galilee and engaged in many battles with the nations; and the nations were crushed before him, and he pursued them as far as the gate
verses.5:22: of Ptolemais; and about three thousand men of the nations fell. And he took their spoils,
verses.5:23: and he took with him those who were in Galilee and in Arbatta, with their wives and children and all that belonged to them, and brought them into Judea with great joy.
verses.5:24: And Judas Maccabeus and Jonathan his brother crossed the Jordan and went a journey of three days through the desert.
verses.5:25: And the Nabateans met them, and received them peacefully, and recounted to them everything that had happened to their brothers in Gilead,
verses.5:26: and that many of them have been trapped in Barasa, Bosor, Alema, Casphor, Mageth, and Carnaim; all these are fortified and great cities.
verses.5:27: Moreover, in the remaining cities of Gilead as well, they are being held trapped, and for tomorrow they have arranged to move up the army against these cities, and to capture and destroy them in one day.
verses.5:28: And Judas and his army suddenly turned their way into the desert of Bosor, and seized the city, and killed every male by the edge of the sword, and took all their spoils, and set it ablaze with fire.
verses.5:29: And they rose up from there by night and went as far as the fortress.
verses.5:30: And it happened at dawn, when they lifted up their eyes, look: a great crowd of people, of whom there was no number, carrying ladders and siege engines to capture the fortress and attack them.
verses.5:31: And Judas saw that the battle had begun, and the cry of battle rose up to heaven like a trumpet, and a great cry from the city,
verses.5:32: and he said to his army, "Fight today for your brothers."
verses.5:33: And he came behind them in three divisions, and they sounded out with trumpets, and cried out in prayer.
verses.5:34: And the camp of Timothy recognized that it was Maccabeus, and they fled before him; and they struck them with a great blow. And about eight thousand men from among them fell on that day.
verses.5:35: And Judas turned aside to Mizpah, and attacked and captured it; and he killed every male in it, and took its spoils, and set it ablaze with fire.
verses.5:36: From there he proceeded and captured Casbon, Mageth, Bosor, and the remaining cities of Gilead.
verses.5:37: Now after these things Timothy gathered another army and pitched camp opposite Raphon across the stream.
verses.5:38: And Judas sent men to scout the army; and they reported back to him, saying, "All the nations that are around us have assembled to him, an exceedingly large army,
verses.5:39: and they have hired Arabs to help them, and they have pitched camp across the stream, ready to come against you in battle." And Judas went to meet them.
verses.5:40: And Timothy said to the commanders of his army, "When Judas and his army draw near to the stream of water, if he crosses over to us first, we will not be able to withstand him, because he will surely prevail against us;
verses.5:41: but if he is afraid to cross over and pitches camp beyond the river, we will cross over to them and prevail against him."
verses.5:42: Now when Judas drew near to the stream of water, he stationed the scribes of the people beside the stream and charged them, saying, "Leave no man behind, but let all come into battle."
verses.5:43: And he crossed over to them first, and all the people after him; and all the nations were crushed before them, and they threw away their weapons and fled to the temple that was in Carnaim.
verses.5:44: And he seized the city itself, and set the temple ablaze with fire, together with all who were in it; and Carnaim was overpowered and could not stand before the face of Judas.
verses.5:45: And Judas gathered together all the Israelites who were in Gilead, from the least to the greatest, and their wives and children, and a very great army, so that they might come into the land of Judah.
verses.5:46: And they came as far as Ephron; and this was a great city situated at the entrance, strongly fortified, and there was no way to turn aside from it to the right or to the left, but the way lay through the middle of it.
verses.5:47: And those who were in the city shut themselves in and blocked up the gates with stones; and Judas sent to them with peaceful words,
verses.5:48: saying, "Let us pass through your land so that we may go into our land; and no one will harm you; we will only pass through on foot." And they were unwilling to open to them.
verses.5:49: And Judas commanded it to be proclaimed in the camp that each one should encamp in the place where he was;
verses.5:50: and the men of valor encamped, and he assaulted that city all day and all night, and the city was delivered into his hand;
verses.5:51: and they put every male to death by the edge of the sword, and he razed it, and took its spoils, and passed through the whole city over those who had been killed.
verses.5:52: And they crossed the Jordan in the great plain, opposite Beth-shan.
verses.5:53: And Judas was gathering those at the rear and encouraging the people along the whole way, until they came into the land of Judah;
verses.5:54: and they went up to Mount Zion with gladness and joy, and offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen until they returned in peace.
verses.5:55: And in the days when Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Gilead, and Simon his brother was in Galilee opposite Ptolemais,
verses.5:56: Joseph the son of Zechariah, and Azariah, commander of the force, heard of the deeds well accomplished and the battles that had taken place,
verses.5:57: and he said, "Let us also make a name for ourselves, and let us go to fight against the nations that are around us."
verses.5:58: And he commanded those who were in his army, and they went to Jamnia.
verses.5:59: And Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
verses.5:60: And Joseph and Azariah were put to flight as far as the borders of Judea; and on that day about two thousand men of the people of Israel fell, and a great rout took place among the people,
verses.5:61: because they did not listen to Judas and his brothers, thinking that they would act bravely.
verses.5:62: However, they themselves were not of the offspring of those men through whom deliverance came about in Israel.
verses.5:63: And the men of Judah were greatly magnified in the sight of all Israel, and of all the nations where their name was heard.
verses.5:64: And people came together to them, shouting joyful acclamations.
verses.5:65: And Judas and his brothers went out and attacked the sons of Esau in the land that is to the south; and he struck Hebron and its daughters, and set its walls and towers all around ablaze with fire.
verses.5:66: And he moved camp to go into the land of the foreigners, and he passed through Samaria.
verses.5:67: On that day priests fell in war, while wishing to act bravely, while going out into battle without counsel.
verses.5:68: And Judas turned aside to Azotus, into the land of the foreigners, and tore down their altars, and set the carved images of their gods ablaze with fire; and he took the spoils of the cities, and returned to the land of Judah.
verses.6:1: And King Antiochus was traveling through the upper regions, and he heard that there was a city, Elymais, in Persia, most renowned and abounding in silver and gold,
verses.6:2: and an exceedingly wealthy temple in it, and that golden coverings, breastplates, and shields were there, which Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian king, who reigned first in Greece, had left behind.
verses.6:3: And he came and sought to capture the city and plunder it, and he could not, because the matter became known to those who were in the city.
verses.6:4: And they rose up for battle, and he fled from there, and departed with great grief, and returned to Babylonia.
verses.6:5: And someone came to report to him in Persia that the armies which were in the land of Judah were put to flight,
verses.6:6: and that Lysias went out with a strong force at first, and was put to flight before the face of the Jews, and they grew strong in weapons, in might, and in many spoils, which they took from the armies that they cut down,
verses.6:7: and that they tore down the abomination which he had built upon the altar that was in Jerusalem, and surrounded the sanctuary with high walls, as before, and also Beth-zur, their city.
verses.6:8: And it happened that when the king heard these words, he was terrified and greatly shaken; and he fell onto his bed and fell into sickness from grief, because it did not happen for him as he had planned.
verses.6:9: And he was there for many days, because great grief was renewed in him, and he thought that he was dying.
verses.6:10: And he called all his friends and said to them, "Sleep has departed from my eyes, and I have fallen and collapsed in heart from anxiety;
verses.6:11: and I said in my heart, 'Into what great tribulation I have come, and into what waves of grief, in which I now am, I who was cheerful and beloved in my power!'
verses.6:12: But now I remember the evils that I did in Jerusalem, from which I also took away all the golden and silver spoils that were in it, and I sent to remove the inhabitants of Judea without cause.
verses.6:13: Therefore I know that for this reason these evils have found me; and look, I am perishing from great grief in a foreign land."
verses.6:14: And he called Philip, one of his friends, and set him over his entire kingdom,
verses.6:15: and gave him the diadem, his robe, and the ring, so that he might bring his son Antiochus, and raise him, and that he might reign.
verses.6:16: And King Antiochus died there in the one hundred and forty-ninth year.
verses.6:17: And Lysias learned that the king had died, and he appointed his son Antiochus, whom he had raised as a youth, to reign; and he called his name Eupator.
verses.6:18: And those who were in the citadel had shut Israel in around the holy places, and were always seeking harm for them and support for the Gentiles.
verses.6:19: And Judas planned to destroy them, and he summoned the entire people so that they might besiege them.
verses.6:20: And they gathered together and besieged them in the one hundred and fiftieth year, and they made catapults and siege engines.
verses.6:21: And some of those who were being besieged went out, and some ungodly men from Israel joined themselves to them,
verses.6:22: and they went to the king and said, "How long will you not execute judgment and avenge our brothers?
verses.6:23: We resolved to serve your father, and to walk in his precepts, and to obey his edicts;
verses.6:24: and because of this the sons of our people were estranging themselves from us, and whoever of us was found was killed, and our inheritances were plundered.
verses.6:25: And they have stretched out their hand not only against us, but also against all our borders;
verses.6:26: and look, today they have encamped against the citadel of Jerusalem to seize it, and they have fortified the fortress of Beth-zur;
verses.6:27: and unless you forestall them quickly, they will do greater things than these, and you will not be able to restrain them."
verses.6:28: And the king became angry when he heard these things, and he summoned all his friends, and the commanders of his army, and those who were over the horsemen;
verses.6:29: and also from other kingdoms and from the islands of the sea, mercenary armies came to him.
verses.6:30: And the number of his army was one hundred thousand foot soldiers, and twenty thousand horsemen, and thirty-two elephants, trained for battle.
verses.6:31: And they came through Idumea, and encamped against Beth-zur, and fought for many days; and they made siege engines, and they came out and burned them with fire, and fought bravely.
verses.6:32: And Judas withdrew from the citadel, and moved camp to Beth-zechariah, opposite the camp of the king.
verses.6:33: And the king rose before dawn, and urged the armies into a charge toward the road to Beth-zechariah; and the armies prepared themselves for battle, and sounded the trumpets;
verses.6:34: and to the elephants they showed the blood of grapes and mulberries, to incite them for battle;
verses.6:35: and they divided the beasts among the legions, and beside each elephant stood a thousand men in linked coats of mail, and bronze helmets were on their heads; and five hundred selected horsemen were assigned to each beast.
verses.6:36: These were there ahead of time wherever the beast was, and wherever it went, they went, and they did not depart from it.
verses.6:37: And also sturdy wooden towers were upon them, giving protection upon each beast, and upon them were engines, and upon each one were thirty-two men of valor who fought from above, and the Indian master of the beast.
verses.6:38: And he stationed the rest of the cavalry on this side and on that in two divisions, to rouse the army with trumpets and to press forward those packed closely together in his legions.
verses.6:39: And when the sun shone upon the golden and bronze shields, the mountains gleamed from them, and they gleamed like torches of fire.
verses.6:40: And part of the king's army was divided across the high mountains, and another part across the low places; and they marched cautiously and in order.
verses.6:41: And all the inhabitants of the land were shaken at the sound of the multitude, and the marching of the throng, and the clashing of weapons; for the army was exceedingly great and strong.
verses.6:42: And Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men from the king's army fell.
verses.6:43: And Eleazar, son of Saura, saw one of the beasts armored with the king's armor, and it towered above the other beasts, and it seemed to him that the king was on it;
verses.6:44: and he gave himself so that he might deliver his people and gain for himself an everlasting name.
verses.6:45: And he ran boldly toward it in the midst of the legion, killing on the right and on the left, and they fell before him on this side and on that.
verses.6:46: And he went under the feet of the elephant, and placed himself beneath it, and killed it; and it fell to the ground upon him, and he died there.
verses.6:47: And seeing the might of the king and the charge of his army, they turned away from them.
verses.6:48: Now the armies of the king went up against them to Jerusalem, and the armies of the king encamped against Judea and Mount Zion.
verses.6:49: And he made peace with those who were in Beth-zur; and they came out of the city, because there were no provisions for them there while they were shut in, because it was a sabbath for the land.
verses.6:50: And the king took Beth-zur, and stationed a garrison there to guard it.
verses.6:51: And he turned his camp against the place of the sanctuary for many days, and he set up there catapults, and siege engines, and missiles of fire, and engines for hurling stones, and javelins, and scorpions for shooting arrows, and slings.
verses.6:52: But they themselves also made siege engines against their siege engines, and they fought for many days.
verses.6:53: But there was no food in the city, because it was the seventh year, and those who had remained in Judea from among the Gentiles had consumed their remaining stores, which had been laid up.
verses.6:54: And few men remained in the holy places, because famine had overpowered them; and they were scattered, each one to his own place.
verses.6:55: And Lysias heard that Philip, whom King Antiochus had appointed while he was still alive to raise his son Antiochus and that he might reign,
verses.6:56: had returned from Persia and Media, along with the army that had gone with him, and that he was seeking to take over the affairs of the kingdom.
verses.6:57: He hastened to go and say to the king and to the leaders of the army, "We are failing daily, and our food is scant, and the place that we are besieging is fortified, and it falls upon us to set the kingdom in order.
verses.6:58: Now therefore let us give our right hands to these men, and let us make peace with them and with all their nation,
verses.6:59: and let us decree for them that they may walk in their laws as before; for because of their own laws, which we despised, they became angry and did all these things."
verses.6:60: And the word was pleasing in the sight of the king and the commanders; and he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted it.
verses.6:61: And the king and the commanders swore to them, and they came out of the fortress.
verses.6:62: And the king entered Mount Zion, and saw the fortification of the place; and he quickly broke the oath that he had sworn, and gave orders to destroy the wall all around.
verses.6:63: And he departed hastily, and returned to Antioch, and found Philip ruling over the city; and he fought against him and seized the city.
verses.7:1: In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius, the son of Seleucus, went out from the city of Rome, and went up with a few men into a coastal city, and reigned there.
verses.7:2: And it happened that, as he entered the house of the kingdom of his fathers, the army seized Antiochus and Lysias so that they might bring them to him.
verses.7:3: And the matter became known to him, and he said, "Do not show me their faces."
verses.7:4: And the army killed them. And Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
verses.7:5: And wicked and ungodly men from Israel came to him, and their leader was Alcimus, who wanted to be made priest.
verses.7:6: And they accused the people before the king, saying, "Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your friends, and he has scattered us from our land.
verses.7:7: Now therefore, send a man whom you trust, so that he may go and see all the destruction that he has done to us and to the regions of the king, and punish all his friends and their helpers."
verses.7:8: And the king chose from among his friends Bacchides, who ruled beyond the great river in the kingdom and was faithful to the king, and he sent him,
verses.7:9: so that he might see the destruction that Judas had done; and he also appointed the ungodly Alcimus to the priesthood, and commanded him to take vengeance on the sons of Israel.
verses.7:10: And they arose and came with a great army into the land of Judah, and they sent messengers and spoke to Judas and to his brothers with peaceful words in deceit.
verses.7:11: And they did not pay attention to their words, for they saw that they had come with a great army.
verses.7:12: And an assembly of scribes came together to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek what is just,
verses.7:13: and the first were the Hasideans who were among the sons of Israel, and they sought peace from them.
verses.7:14: For they said, "A man who is a priest from the seed of Aaron has come; he will not deceive us."
verses.7:15: And he spoke peaceful words with them, and swore to them, saying, "We will not bring harm upon you, nor upon your friends."
verses.7:16: And they trusted him; and he seized sixty men from among them and killed them in one day, according to the word that is written:
verses.7:17: "The flesh of Your holy ones and their blood they poured out around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
verses.7:18: And fear and trembling fell upon all the people, for they said, "There is no truth or justice in them, for they have transgressed the agreement and the oath that they swore."
verses.7:19: And Bacchides moved camp from Jerusalem and encamped at Bethzecha; and he sent and seized many of those who had fled from him, and he slaughtered some of the people and threw them into a great pit.
verses.7:20: And he entrusted the region to Alcimus, and left a force with him to assist him. And Bacchides departed to the king.
verses.7:21: And Alcimus strove earnestly for the leadership of his priesthood,
verses.7:22: and all who were troubling their own people came together to him, and they gained control of the land of Judah and inflicted a great blow in Israel.
verses.7:23: And Judas saw all the evils that Alcimus and those who were with him had done to the sons of Israel, much more than the nations,
verses.7:24: and he went out into all the borders of Judea all around, and executed vengeance on the men who were deserters, and they stopped going out any longer into the region.
verses.7:25: Now Alcimus saw that Judas and those who were with him had prevailed, and he realized that he could not withstand them; and he returned to the king and accused them of many crimes.
verses.7:26: And the king sent Nicanor, one of his more noble princes, who was pursuing enmity against Israel, and he commanded him to overthrow the people.
verses.7:27: And Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great army, and he sent to Judas and to his brothers with peaceful words, with deceit,
verses.7:28: saying, "Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, so that I may see your faces in peace."
verses.7:29: And he came to Judas, and they greeted one another peacefully; and the enemies were ready to carry off Judas.
verses.7:30: And the report became known to Judas that he had come to him with deceit, and he was terrified of him and did not want to see his face any longer.
verses.7:31: And Nicanor realized that his plan had been laid bare, and he went out to meet Judas in battle near Capharsalama.
verses.7:32: And about five thousand men of Nicanor's army fell, and they fled into the city of David.
verses.7:33: And after these things, Nicanor went up to Mount Zion; and some of the priests of the people went out to greet him in peace and to show him the burnt offerings that were being offered for the king.
verses.7:34: And mocking them, he despised them and defiled them, and spoke arrogantly,
verses.7:35: and swore in anger, saying, "Unless Judas and his army are handed over into my hands, as soon as I return in peace, I will burn down this house." And he went out in great anger.
verses.7:36: And the priests entered and stood in front of the altar and the temple, and weeping, they said,
verses.7:37: "You, Lord, chose this house for Your name to be called upon in it, so that it might be a house of prayer and supplication for Your people.
verses.7:38: Execute vengeance on this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword; remember their blasphemies, and do not grant that they remain."
verses.7:39: And Nicanor went out from Jerusalem and pitched camp at Beth-horon, and an army of Syria met him.
verses.7:40: And Judas encamped at Adarsa with three thousand men; and Judas prayed and said,
verses.7:41: "Lord, because those who had been sent by King Sennacherib blasphemed You, an angel went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand of them;
verses.7:42: so crush this army in our sight today, and let the rest know that he has spoken evil against Your holy places, and judge him according to his wickedness."
verses.7:43: And the armies joined battle on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar; and the camp of Nicanor was crushed, and he himself fell first in the battle.
verses.7:44: Now when his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw away their weapons and fled;
verses.7:45: and they pursued them a day's journey from Adazer until one comes to Gazara, and they sounded trumpets after them with signals;
verses.7:46: and they went out from all the villages of Judea all around, and tossed them with horns, and they were turned back again toward them, and they all fell by the sword, and not even one of them was left.
verses.7:47: And they took their spoils as plunder, and they cut off the head of Nicanor and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and hung them up opposite Jerusalem.
verses.7:48: And the people rejoiced greatly, and they kept that day in great joy.
verses.7:49: And he decreed that this day be kept every year on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar.
verses.7:50: And the land of Judah was quiet for a few days.
verses.8:1: And Judas heard the name of the Romans, that they are mighty in strength, and consent to all things that are requested of them, and whoever approached them established friendships with them, and that they are mighty in strength.
verses.8:2: And they heard of their battles and the good deeds of valor that they performed in Galatia, that they conquered them and brought them under tribute;
verses.8:3: and what great things they did in the region of Spain, and that they brought under their power the mines of silver and gold that are there, and took possession of the entire place by their counsel and patience,
verses.8:4: and the places that were very far from them; and they crushed the kings who had come against them from the ends of the earth, and struck them with a great blow; but the rest give them tribute every year.
verses.8:5: And in war they crushed Philip and Perseus, king of the Kittim, and the others who had taken up arms against them, and conquered them;
verses.8:6: and that Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, who had waged battle against them, having one hundred twenty elephants, and cavalry, and chariots, and a very great army, was crushed by them;
verses.8:7: and that they captured him alive, and decreed for him that he himself, and those who would reign after him, should give a great tribute, and that he should give hostages, and a settlement,
verses.8:8: and the region of the Indians, and the Medes, and the Lydians, from their best regions; and having received them from them, they gave them to King Eumenes;
verses.8:9: and that those who were in Greece wanted to go and do away with them, and the word became known to them,
verses.8:10: and they sent one commander to them, and fought against them, and many of them fell, and they led their wives and children away captive, and plundered them, and took possession of their land, and tore down their walls, and brought them into servitude to this day;
verses.8:11: and they destroyed the remaining kingdoms and islands that had at any time resisted them, and brought them under their power.
verses.8:12: But with their friends and those who had rest in them, they preserved friendship, and they conquered the kingdoms that were near and those that were far; for whoever heard their name feared them;
verses.8:13: indeed, those whom they wished to help, so that they might reign, reigned; while those whom they wished, they cast down from the kingdom; and they were greatly exalted.
verses.8:14: And in all these things no one wore a diadem, nor was clothed in purple so that he might be magnified in it.
verses.8:15: And that they made a senate house for themselves, and daily they consulted three hundred twenty men, always taking counsel concerning the multitude, so that they may carry out the things that are worthy;
verses.8:16: and they entrust their magistracy to one man each year to rule over their entire land, and all obey one, and there is neither envy nor jealousy among them.
verses.8:17: And Judas chose Eupolemus, the son of John, the son of Jacob, and Jason, the son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish friendship and an alliance with them,
verses.8:18: and so that they might remove from them the yoke of the Greeks, because they saw that they were pressing the kingdom of Israel into servitude.
verses.8:19: And they went to Rome, a very long journey, and entered the senate house, and said:
verses.8:20: "Judas Maccabeus, and his brothers, and the people of the Jews have sent us to you to establish an alliance and peace with you, and to enroll us as your allies and friends."
verses.8:21: And the word was pleasing in their sight.
verses.8:22: And this is the copy that they wrote in reply on bronze tablets, and sent to Jerusalem, so that it might be with them there as a memorial of peace and alliance:
verses.8:23: "May it be well with the Romans and with the nation of the Jews at sea and on land forever; and may sword and enemy be far from them.
verses.8:24: Now if war comes upon the Romans first, or upon all their allies in all their dominion,
verses.8:25: the nation of the Jews will bring help, as the time dictates, with a full heart;
verses.8:26: and to those waging battle they will not give nor supply wheat, arms, money, ships, as it has pleased the Romans; and they will keep their commands, receiving nothing from them.
verses.8:27: Likewise also, if war comes upon the nation of the Jews first, the Romans will help from the heart, as the time permits them;
verses.8:28: and to those who help there will not be given wheat, arms, money, ships, as it has pleased the Romans; and they will keep their commands without deceit.
verses.8:29: According to these words the Romans have established it for the people of the Jews.
verses.8:30: Now if after these words the one party or the other wishes to add anything to these things or take anything away from them, they will do so according to their own purpose; and whatever they add or take away will be valid.
verses.8:31: Moreover, concerning the evils that King Demetrius has done against them, we have written to him, saying, 'Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies, the Jews?
verses.8:32: If therefore they appeal to us again, we will render judgment for them against you, and we will fight against you by sea and by land.'"
verses.9:1: Meanwhile, when Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his army had fallen in battle, he proceeded to send Bacchides and Alcimus into Judea again, and the right wing with them.
verses.9:2: And they went by the road that leads to Gilgal, and pitched camp at Masaloth, which is in Arbela; and they captured it and destroyed many human lives.
verses.9:3: In the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year, they brought the army up to Jerusalem.
verses.9:4: And they rose up and went to Berea, twenty thousand men and two thousand horsemen.
verses.9:5: And Judas had pitched camp at Laisa, and three thousand chosen men were with him.
verses.9:6: And they saw the multitude of the army, that they were many, and they were greatly afraid; and many withdrew from the camp, and none of them remained except eight hundred men.
verses.9:7: And Judas saw that his army had melted away and the battle was pressing hard upon him, and he was crushed in heart because he had no time to gather them, and he grew faint.
verses.9:8: And he said to those who remained, "Let us rise up and go against our adversaries, to see if we will be able to fight against them."
verses.9:9: And they tried to turn him back, saying, "We will not be able, but let us save our lives now and return to our brothers, and then we will fight against them; we, however, are few."
verses.9:10: And Judas said, "May it be far from us to do this thing, that we should flee from them; and if our time has drawn near, let us die in valor for the sake of our brothers, and let us not bring a reproach upon our glory."
verses.9:11: And the army moved out from the camp, and they stood to meet them; and the horsemen were divided into two divisions, and the slingers and archers went ahead of the army, and the foremost of the battle were all mighty men.
verses.9:12: Now Bacchides was on the right wing, and the legion drew near from both sides, and they sounded the trumpets.
verses.9:13: And those who were on the side of Judas also cried out themselves, and the earth was shaken by the sound of the armies; and the battle was fought from morning until evening.
verses.9:14: And Judas saw that the stronger part of the army of Bacchides was on the right, and all who were steadfast in heart came together with him.
verses.9:15: And the right part was crushed by them, and he pursued them as far as Mount Azotus.
verses.9:16: And those who were on the left wing saw that the right wing had been crushed, and they followed after Judas and those who were with him from the rear.
verses.9:17: And the battle grew heavy, and many fell wounded on this side and on that.
verses.9:18: And Judas fell, and the rest fled.
verses.9:19: And Jonathan and Simon took Judas their brother and buried him in the tomb of their fathers in the city of Modin.
verses.9:20: And all the people of Israel wept for him with great lamentation, and they mourned for many days,
verses.9:21: and said, "How the mighty one has fallen, who saved the people of Israel!"
verses.9:22: And the rest of the accounts of the wars of Judas, and of the deeds of valor that he performed, and of his greatness, have not been written down; for they were very many.
verses.9:23: And it happened that after the death of Judas, wicked men emerged within all the borders of Israel, and all who practiced wickedness sprang up.
verses.9:24: In those days there came a very great famine, and their whole region handed itself over to Bacchides along with them.
verses.9:25: And Bacchides chose ungodly men and appointed them masters of the region.
verses.9:26: And they sought out and searched thoroughly for the friends of Judas, and brought them to Bacchides, and he took vengeance on them and mocked them.
verses.9:27: And there came great tribulation in Israel, such as had not been since the day a prophet was no longer seen in Israel.
verses.9:28: And all the friends of Judas gathered together and said to Jonathan,
verses.9:29: "Since your brother Judas died, there is no man like him to go out against our enemies, Bacchides and those who are enemies of our nation.
verses.9:30: Now therefore, we have chosen you today to be in his place for us as ruler and leader, to fight our war."
verses.9:31: And Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and rose up in place of Judas his brother.
verses.9:32: And Bacchides learned of it and sought to kill him.
verses.9:33: And Jonathan, and Simon his brother, and all who were with him learned of it; and they fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and camped by the water of the pool of Asphar.
verses.9:34: And Bacchides learned of it, and on the Sabbath day he himself and all his army came across the Jordan.
verses.9:35: And Jonathan sent his brother, the leader of the people, and asked the Nabateans, his friends, that they might lend them their equipment, which was abundant.
verses.9:36: And the sons of Jambri came out from Medeba, and seized John and all that he had, and went away with them in their possession.
verses.9:37: After these things, it was reported to Jonathan and to Simon his brother that the sons of Jambri were holding a great wedding and were bringing the bride from Medeba, the daughter of one of the great rulers of Canaan, with great pomp.
verses.9:38: And they remembered the blood of John their brother, and they went up and hid themselves under the cover of the mountain.
verses.9:39: And they lifted up their eyes and saw, and look, there was a commotion and much equipment; and the bridegroom came out, and his friends and his brothers, to meet them with tambourines and musical instruments and many weapons.
verses.9:40: And they rose up against them from ambush and killed them, and many fell wounded, and those who remained fled into the mountains; and they took all their spoils.
verses.9:41: And the wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musical instruments into lament.
verses.9:42: And they took vengeance for the blood of their brother, and returned to the bank of the Jordan.
verses.9:43: And Bacchides heard of it, and came on the Sabbath day as far as the edge of the Jordan with a great force.
verses.9:44: And Jonathan said to his men, "Let us rise up and fight against our enemies, for today is not like yesterday and the day before;
verses.9:45: for look, the battle is in front of us, and the water of the Jordan is on this side and on that, and the banks, and the marshes, and the thickets; and there is no place to turn aside.
verses.9:46: Now therefore, cry out to heaven, that you may be delivered from the hand of your enemies." And the battle was joined.
verses.9:47: And Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, and he turned back away from him.
verses.9:48: And Jonathan and those who were with him leaped into the Jordan, and they swam across the Jordan to them.
verses.9:49: And one thousand men fell on the side of Bacchides on that day. And they returned to Jerusalem,
verses.9:50: and built fortified cities in Judea: the fortress that was in Jericho, and in Emmaus, and in Beth-horon, and in Bethel, and Timnath, and Phara, and Thopo, with high walls and gates and bars.
verses.9:51: And he placed a garrison in them, that they might carry on hostilities against Israel.
verses.9:52: And he fortified the city of Beth-zur, and Gazara, and the citadel, and placed troops in them and a supply of food.
verses.9:53: And he took the sons of the rulers of the region as hostages and placed them in the citadel in Jerusalem under guard.
verses.9:54: And in the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus commanded the walls of the inner holy house to be torn down, and the works of the prophets to be torn down; and he began to tear them down.
verses.9:55: At that time Alcimus was stricken, and his works were hindered, and his mouth was shut, and he was disabled by paralysis, and he could no longer speak a word or give instructions concerning his house.
verses.9:56: And Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
verses.9:57: And Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died, and he returned to the king. And the land was quiet for two years.
verses.9:58: And all the wicked men plotted, saying, "Look, Jonathan and those who are with him are living in quiet and confidence; now therefore, let us bring Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night."
verses.9:59: And they went and gave him counsel.
verses.9:60: And he rose up to come with a large army, and secretly sent letters to his allies who were in Judea, that they should seize Jonathan and those who were with him; but they could not, because their plan became known to them.
verses.9:61: And from among the men of the region who were leaders of the wickedness, he seized fifty men and killed them.
verses.9:62: And Jonathan, and Simon, and those who were with him withdrew to Bethbessen, which is in the wilderness; and he rebuilt its ruins, and they fortified it.
verses.9:63: And Bacchides learned of it, and gathered together his entire multitude, and sent word to those who were from Judea.
verses.9:64: And he came and pitched camp above Bethbessen, and attacked it for many days, and made siege engines.
verses.9:65: And Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city, and went out into the region, and came with a number of men.
verses.9:66: And he struck Odaren and his brothers, and the sons of Phaseron in their tents; and he began to cut them down and to grow in forces.
verses.9:67: Now Simon and those who were with him went out from the city and set fire to the siege engines,
verses.9:68: and fought against Bacchides, and he was crushed by them; and they distressed him greatly, because his plan and his assault were in vain.
verses.9:69: And enraged against the wicked men who had given him counsel to come into their region, he killed many of them; and he himself planned to go away with the rest to his own region.
verses.9:70: And Jonathan learned of it, and he sent envoys to him to make peace with him and to return the captives to him.
verses.9:71: And he gladly accepted and did according to his words, and swore that he would do him no harm all the days of his life.
verses.9:72: And he returned to him the captives whom he had previously taken as plunder from the land of Judah; and he turned back and went away to his own land, and did not proceed to come into its borders any longer.
verses.9:73: And the sword ceased from Israel; and Jonathan lived in Michmash, and there Jonathan began to judge the people, and he wiped out the ungodly from Israel.
verses.10:1: And in the one hundred and sixtieth year, Alexander, the son of Antiochus, who was surnamed the Noble, went up and occupied Ptolemais; and they received him, and he reigned there.
verses.10:2: And King Demetrius heard, and gathered a very large army, and went out to meet him in battle.
verses.10:3: And Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan with peaceful words, so as to exalt him.
verses.10:4: For he said, "Let us act first to make peace with him, before he does so with Alexander against us;
verses.10:5: for he will remember all the evils that we have done against him, and against his brother, and against his nation."
verses.10:6: And he gave him authority to gather an army, and to manufacture weapons, and himself to be his ally; and he ordered the hostages who were in the citadel to be handed over to him.
verses.10:7: And Jonathan came into Jerusalem, and read the letters in the hearing of all the people, and of those who were in the citadel.
verses.10:8: And they feared with a great fear, because they heard that the king had given him authority to gather an army.
verses.10:9: And the hostages were handed over to Jonathan, and he returned them to their parents;
verses.10:10: and Jonathan lived in Jerusalem, and began to build and renew the city.
verses.10:11: And he told those doing the work to build up the walls, and Mount Zion all around with squared stones for fortification; and they did so.
verses.10:12: And the foreigners who were in the fortresses that Bacchides had built fled;
verses.10:13: and each one left his place and went away to his own land;
verses.10:14: only in Beth-zur did some remain of those who had abandoned the law and the precepts of God, for it was a refuge for them.
verses.10:15: And King Alexander heard the promises that Demetrius had promised to Jonathan; and they recounted to him the battles, and the valiant deeds that he himself and his brothers had done, and the toils through which they had labored;
verses.10:16: and he said, "Will we find any such man? And now we will make him our friend and ally."
verses.10:17: And he wrote a letter and sent it to him according to these words, saying:
verses.10:18: "King Alexander, to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
verses.10:19: We have heard about you that you are a man mighty in strength, and you are fit to be our friend;
verses.10:20: and now we appoint you today high priest of your nation, and to be called the king's friend" (and he sent him a purple robe and a golden crown) "and to be of one mind with us in our affairs, and to preserve friendship toward us."
verses.10:21: And Jonathan clothed himself in the holy robe in the seventh month, in the one hundred and sixtieth year, on the festival day of Tabernacles; and he gathered an army and made weapons in abundance.
