verses.10:22: And Demetrius heard these words, and was greatly grieved, and said,
verses.10:23: "Why have we done this, that Alexander has gotten ahead of us to secure the friendship of the Jews for his own defense?
verses.10:24: I also will write to them words of appeal, and honors, and gifts, so that they may be with me as a help."
verses.10:25: And he wrote to them in these words: "King Demetrius, to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.10:26: Because you have kept the pact with us, and have remained in our friendship, and have not gone over to our enemies, we have heard and have rejoiced.
verses.10:27: And now continue still to keep faith with us, and we will repay you good things for what you have done with us;
verses.10:28: and we will remit for you many dues, and we will give you grants.
verses.10:29: And now I release you and all the Jews from tributes, and I waive the prices of salt, and I remit the crowns, and the thirds of the seed;
verses.10:30: and half of the fruit of the tree, which is of my portion, I leave to you from this day onward, so that it may not be taken from the land of Judah and from the three cities that were added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time;
verses.10:31: and let Jerusalem be holy and free, with its borders, and let the tithes and tributes be its own.
verses.10:32: I also relinquish authority over the citadel that is in Jerusalem, and I give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it whichever men he himself chooses to guard it.
verses.10:33: And every soul of the Jews who is captive from the land of Judah in all my kingdom I leave free without charge, so that all may be released from tributes, even those of their livestock.
verses.10:34: And all the festival days, and the Sabbaths, and the new moons, and the appointed days, and three days before a festival day, and three days after a festival day, let all of them be days of immunity and remission for all the Jews who are in my kingdom;
verses.10:35: and no one will have authority to take any action or stir up trouble against any of them in any case.
verses.10:36: And let there be enrolled from among the Jews in the king's army up to thirty thousand men; and provisions will be given to them as is proper for all the armies of the king, and some of them will be assigned to be in the fortresses of the great king;
verses.10:37: and some of these will be appointed over the affairs of the kingdom that are conducted in trust, and let commanders be from among them, and let them walk in their own laws, just as the king has commanded in the land of Judah.
verses.10:38: And let the three cities that were added to Judea from the region of Samaria be reckoned with Judea, so that they may be under one, and not obey any other authority except that of the high priest.
verses.10:39: Ptolemais and its bordering territories, these I have given as a gift to the holy ones who are in Jerusalem, for the necessary expenses of the sanctuary.
verses.10:40: And I give each year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king's accounts that belong to me;
verses.10:41: and all that remains, which those who were over the affairs had not paid in previous years, they will give from now on for the works of the house.
verses.10:42: And in addition to these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to collect from the account of the sanctuary each year: let these also belong to the priests who perform the ministry.
verses.10:43: And all who take refuge in the temple that is in Jerusalem and within all its borders, being liable to the king in any matter, let them be released, and let them hold free all that is theirs in my kingdom.
verses.10:44: And for building or restoring the works of the sanctuary, the expenses will be given from the king's account;
verses.10:45: and for building up the walls of Jerusalem and fortifying them all around, the expenses will be given from the king's account, and for constructing the walls in Judea."
verses.10:46: Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, they did not believe them, nor did they accept them, because they remembered the great wickedness that he had done in Israel, and he had greatly afflicted them.
verses.10:47: And they were well pleased with Alexander, because he himself had been to them the originator of words of peace, and they gave him help all the days.
verses.10:48: And King Alexander gathered a great army, and moved his camp against Demetrius.
verses.10:49: And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued him and pressed hard upon them.
verses.10:50: And the battle grew exceedingly fierce until the sun set, and Demetrius fell on that day.
verses.10:51: And Alexander sent envoys to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, according to these words, saying:
verses.10:52: "Since I have returned to my kingdom, and have sat on the throne of my fathers, and have obtained the rule, and have crushed Demetrius, and have taken possession of our region,
verses.10:53: and have joined battle with him, and he himself and his camp have been crushed by us, and we have sat on the throne of his kingdom;
verses.10:54: and now let us establish friendship with one another; and give me your daughter as a wife, and I will be your son-in-law, and I will give gifts to you, and to her, worthy of you."
verses.10:55: And King Ptolemy answered, saying, "Happy is the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers, and sat on the throne of their kingdom.
verses.10:56: And now I will do for you what you have written; but meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I may make a betrothal with you, just as you have said."
verses.10:57: And Ptolemy went out from Egypt, he himself and Cleopatra his daughter, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
verses.10:58: And King Alexander met him, and he gave him Cleopatra his daughter; and he celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais, as kings do, in great glory.
verses.10:59: And King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come to meet him.
verses.10:60: And he went with glory to Ptolemais, and met the two kings there, and gave them much silver, and gold, and gifts; and he found favor in their sight.
verses.10:61: And pestilent men from Israel assembled against him, lawless men bringing accusations against him; and the king paid no attention to them.
verses.10:62: And he ordered Jonathan to be stripped of his garments and to be clothed in a purple robe; and they did so. And the king placed him to sit with him.
verses.10:63: And he said to his officials, "Go out with him into the middle of the city, and proclaim that no one is to bring an accusation against him concerning any matter, nor is anyone to trouble him on any account."
verses.10:64: And it happened, when those who were bringing accusations saw his glory that was being proclaimed, and him clad in a purple robe, they all fled;
verses.10:65: and the king exalted him, and enrolled him among the first friends, and set him as commander and a sharer in the rule.
verses.10:66: And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladness.
verses.10:67: In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, the son of Demetrius, came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
verses.10:68: And King Alexander heard, and was greatly grieved, and returned to Antioch.
verses.10:69: And King Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria, as commander; and he gathered a great army and approached Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest,
verses.10:70: saying, "You alone resist us; and I have become a mockery and a reproach because you exercise authority against us in the mountains.
verses.10:71: Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us match ourselves against one another there; for with me is the power of wars.
verses.10:72: Ask and learn who I am, and the rest who are a help to me, who also say that your foot cannot stand before our face, because twice your fathers were put to flight in their own land;
verses.10:73: and now how will you be able to withstand the cavalry and so great an army in the plain, where there is no stone, nor rock, nor place to flee?"
verses.10:74: Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, he was stirred in spirit; and he chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem, and Simon his brother met him as a help;
verses.10:75: and they brought their camp up to Joppa, and it shut him out from the city, because a garrison of Apollonius was in Joppa; and he attacked it.
verses.10:76: And those who were in the city, being terrified, opened to him, and Jonathan obtained Joppa.
verses.10:77: And Apollonius heard, and he brought up three thousand horsemen and a large army.
verses.10:78: And he went to Azotus as though making a journey, and immediately went out into the plain, because he had a multitude of horsemen and trusted in them. And Jonathan pursued him to Azotus, and they joined battle.
verses.10:79: And Apollonius left a thousand horsemen in the camp behind them secretly.
verses.10:80: And Jonathan learned that an ambush was behind him; and they surrounded his camp and cast darts at the people from morning until evening.
verses.10:81: But the people stood, just as Jonathan had commanded, and their horses grew weary.
verses.10:82: And Simon brought out his army and engaged against the legion, for the horsemen were exhausted; and they were crushed by him and fled.
verses.10:83: And those who were scattered across the plain fled into Azotus, and entered into Beth-dagon, their idol, so that they might deliver themselves there.
verses.10:84: And Jonathan burned Azotus and the cities that were all around it, and took their spoils; and the temple of Dagon, and all who fled into it, he burned with fire.
verses.10:85: And those who fell by the sword, together with those who were burned, were about eight thousand men.
verses.10:86: And Jonathan moved his camp from there, and brought it up to Ashkelon; and they came out from the city to meet him in great glory.
verses.10:87: And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with his men, having many spoils.
verses.10:88: And it happened, when King Alexander heard these words, he proceeded still further to glorify Jonathan.
verses.10:89: And he sent him a golden clasp, just as is the custom to be given to the kinsmen of kings. And he gave him Ekron and all its borders as a possession.
verses.11:1: And the king of Egypt gathered an army like the sand that is along the shore of the sea, and many ships; and he sought to obtain the kingdom of Alexander by deceit and to add it to his own kingdom.
verses.11:2: And he went out into Syria with peaceful words, and the cities opened to him and came to meet him, because King Alexander had given orders to go out to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
verses.11:3: Now whenever Ptolemy entered a city, he placed garrisons of soldiers in each city.
verses.11:4: And when he drew near to Azotus, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned with fire, and Azotus and the rest of it demolished, and the bodies cast out, and the burial mounds of those who had been killed in the war, which they had made beside the road.
verses.11:5: And they told the king that Jonathan had done these things, so that they might stir up ill will against him; and the king remained silent.
verses.11:6: And Jonathan met the king at Joppa with glory, and they greeted one another, and they slept there.
verses.11:7: And Jonathan went with the king as far as the river that is called Eleutherus, and he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.11:8: Now King Ptolemy obtained dominion over the cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and he was devising evil plans against Alexander.
verses.11:9: And he sent envoys to Demetrius, saying, "Come, let us make a pact between us, and I will give you my daughter, whom Alexander has, and you will reign in your father's kingdom;
verses.11:10: for I regret that I gave him my daughter, for he sought to kill me."
verses.11:11: And he found fault with him because he had coveted his kingdom.
verses.11:12: And he took away his daughter and gave her to Demetrius, and he estranged himself from Alexander, and his enmity became evident.
verses.11:13: And Ptolemy entered Antioch and placed two diadems on his head, those of Egypt and of Asia.
verses.11:14: Now King Alexander was in Cilicia in those times, because those who were in those places were rebelling.
verses.11:15: And Alexander heard, and he came against him to war; and King Ptolemy led out the army and met him with a strong hand, and put him to flight.
verses.11:16: And Alexander fled into Arabia so that he might be protected there, but King Ptolemy was exalted.
verses.11:17: And Zabdiel the Arab took off Alexander's head and sent it to Ptolemy.
verses.11:18: And King Ptolemy died on the third day, and those who were in the strongholds perished at the hands of those who were inside the camps.
verses.11:19: And Demetrius began to reign in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
verses.11:20: In those days Jonathan gathered those who were in Judea so that they might storm the citadel that is in Jerusalem, and they made many siege engines against it.
verses.11:21: And certain wicked men who hated their own nation went to King Demetrius and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.
verses.11:22: And when he heard, he became angry; and immediately he came to Ptolemais and wrote to Jonathan not to besiege the citadel, but to meet him for a conference with haste.
verses.11:23: Now when Jonathan heard, he ordered the siege to continue, and he chose some of the elders of Israel and of the priests, and put himself in danger.
verses.11:24: And he took gold, and silver, and clothing, and many other gifts, and went to the king at Ptolemais; and he found favor in his sight,
verses.11:25: and certain wicked men from his own nation were bringing complaints against him.
verses.11:26: And the king did for him just as those who had been before him had done for him, and he exalted him in the sight of all his friends,
verses.11:27: and he established for him the chief office of the priesthood and whatever other precious things he had previously held, and he made him chief of the friends.
verses.11:28: And Jonathan requested of the king that he make Judea, and the three districts, and Samaria and its bordering territories, exempt from tribute; and he promised him three hundred talents.
verses.11:29: And the king agreed, and he wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things, containing these terms:
verses.11:30: "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan, greetings, and to the nation of the Jews.
verses.11:31: We have sent to you a copy of the letter that we wrote to our father Lasthenes concerning you, so that you may know:
verses.11:32: 'King Demetrius to his father Lasthenes, greetings.
verses.11:33: To the nation of the Jews, our friends and keepers of what is just toward us, we have resolved to do good because of their goodwill that they have toward us.
verses.11:34: Therefore we have established for them that all the territories of Judea, and the three cities, Lydda and Ramathan, which were added to Judea from Samaria, and all their bordering territories, be set apart for all who sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of those things that the king previously received from them each year, and in place of the produce of the land and of the fruit trees.
verses.11:35: And from this time we remit to them the other things of the tithes and tributes that belonged to us; and the salt pans and the crowns that were brought to us,
verses.11:36: all of these we grant to them; and none of these things will be void, from this time and for all time.
verses.11:37: Now therefore take care to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan, and let it be placed on the holy mountain, in a prominent place.'"
verses.11:38: And King Demetrius, seeing that the land was quiet in his sight and nothing resisted him, dismissed his entire army, each one to his own place, except the foreign army that he had drawn together from the islands of the nations; and all the armies of his fathers were hostile to him.
verses.11:39: Now Trypho was formerly one of Alexander's party; and he saw that the entire army was grumbling against Demetrius, and he went to Emalchuel the Arab, who was raising Antiochus, the son of Alexander;
verses.11:40: and he stayed persistently with him so that he would hand him over to him, that he might reign in place of his father; and he told him all that Demetrius had done, and the enmity of his armies against him. And he remained there many days.
verses.11:41: And Jonathan sent to King Demetrius that he should drive out those who were in the citadel in Jerusalem and those who were in the garrisons, because they were fighting against Israel.
verses.11:42: And Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying, "Not only will I do these things for you and for your nation, but I will make you and your nation renowned with glory when it is opportune.
verses.11:43: Now therefore you will do well if you send men to my aid, because my entire army has departed."
verses.11:44: And Jonathan sent him three thousand valiant men to Antioch; and they came to the king, and the king was delighted at their arrival.
verses.11:45: And those who were of the city assembled, one hundred and twenty thousand men, and they wanted to kill the king.
verses.11:46: And the king fled into the palace, and those who were of the city seized the streets of the city and began to fight.
verses.11:47: And the king called the Jews to his aid, and they all assembled together to him, and they all dispersed throughout the city;
verses.11:48: and they killed on that day one hundred thousand people, and they set fire to the city, and took much plunder on that day, and rescued the king.
verses.11:49: And those who were of the city saw that the Jews had gained control of the city just as they wanted, and they grew weak in their mind, and cried out to the king with pleas, saying,
verses.11:50: "Give us your right hand, and let the Jews stop attacking us and the city."
verses.11:51: And they threw down their weapons and made peace, and the Jews were glorified in the sight of the king and in the sight of all who were in his kingdom, and they became renowned in the kingdom; and they returned to Jerusalem having much plunder.
verses.11:52: And King Demetrius sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet in his sight.
verses.11:53: And he proved false to all that he had said, and estranged himself from Jonathan, and did not repay him according to the benefits that he had bestowed on him, and he greatly harassed him.
verses.11:54: Now after these things Trypho returned, and with him Antiochus, a young boy, and he began to reign and placed the diadem on himself.
verses.11:55: And all the armies that Demetrius had dispersed gathered to him, and they fought against him, and he fled and turned his back.
verses.11:56: And Trypho took the beasts and gained control of Antioch.
verses.11:57: And the young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, "I establish for you the priesthood, and I appoint you over the four cities, so that you may be among the friends of the king."
verses.11:58: And he sent him gold vessels for service, and gave him authority to drink from gold, and to be in purple, and to have a gold clasp;
verses.11:59: and he appointed his brother Simon commander from the borders of Tyre as far as the boundaries of Egypt.
verses.11:60: And Jonathan went out and traveled through the cities beyond the river, and the entire army of Syria gathered to him to his aid; and he came to Ashkelon, and those from the city met him with honor.
verses.11:61: And he went from there to Gaza, and those who were in Gaza shut themselves in; and he besieged it, and set fire to the things that were around the city and plundered them.
verses.11:62: And the people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he gave them his right hand; and he took their sons as hostages and sent them to Jerusalem; and he traveled through the region as far as Damascus.
verses.11:63: And Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had transgressed in Kedesh, which is in Galilee, with a large army, wishing to remove him from the business of the kingdom;
verses.11:64: and he went to meet them, while he left his brother Simon within the province.
verses.11:65: And Simon encamped against Beth-zur and assaulted it for many days, and shut them in.
verses.11:66: And they requested to receive the right hand from him, and he gave it to them; and he drove them out from there, and took the city, and placed a garrison in it.
verses.11:67: And Jonathan and his forces encamped by the water of Gennesar, and before dawn they kept watch in the plain of Hazor;
verses.11:68: and look, the forces of the foreigners were coming to meet him in the plain, and they were laying an ambush for him in the mountains; but he himself met them from the opposite side.
verses.11:69: Now the ambushers rose up from their places and joined battle.
verses.11:70: And all those who were on Jonathan's side fled, and no one was left of them except Mattathias, the son of Absalom, and Judas, the son of Chalphi, commander of the troops of the army.
verses.11:71: And Jonathan tore his garments, and put earth on his head, and prayed.
verses.11:72: And Jonathan turned back to them into battle, and turned them to flight, and they fought.
verses.11:73: And those of his side who were fleeing saw it and returned to him, and they all pursued with him as far as Kedesh, to their camp, and they reached all the way there;
verses.11:74: and three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day; and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
verses.12:1: And Jonathan saw that the time favored him, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to establish and renew friendship with them.
verses.12:2: And to the Spartans and to other places he sent letters according to the same form.
verses.12:3: And they went to Rome and entered the senate house, and they said, "Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews have sent us so that we might renew friendship and alliance as before."
verses.12:4: And they gave them letters to those in each place, so that they would escort them into the land of Judah in peace.
verses.12:5: And this is the copy of the letters that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
verses.12:6: "Jonathan the high priest, and the elders of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to the Spartan brothers, greetings.
verses.12:7: Long ago letters had been sent to Onias the high priest from Arius, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brothers, just as the copy that is appended below contains.
verses.12:8: And Onias welcomed with honor the man who had been sent, and he received the letters in which declaration was made concerning alliance and friendship.
verses.12:9: Although we had no need of any of these things, having for comfort the holy books that are in our hands,
verses.12:10: we preferred to send to you to renew brotherhood and friendship, so that we might not by chance become estranged from you; for many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
verses.12:11: We therefore at every time without ceasing, on festival days and on the other days on which it is proper, are mindful of you in the sacrifices that we offer and in the observances, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.
verses.12:12: Therefore we rejoice over your glory.
verses.12:13: But many afflictions and many battles have surrounded us, and the kings who are all around us have fought against us.
verses.12:14: Therefore we did not wish to be burdensome to you, nor to our other allies and friends, in these battles;
verses.12:15: for we had help from heaven, and we ourselves were delivered, and our enemies were humbled.
verses.12:16: Therefore we chose Numenius the son of Antiochus and Antipater the son of Jason, and we sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
verses.12:17: Therefore we instructed them to come to you also, and to greet you, and to deliver to you our letters concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
verses.12:18: And now you will do well in answering us regarding these things."
verses.12:19: And this is the copy of the letters that he had sent to Onias:
verses.12:20: "Arius, king of the Spartans, to Onias the great priest, greetings.
verses.12:21: It has been found in a writing concerning the Spartans and the Jews that they are brothers, and that they are of the lineage of Abraham.
verses.12:22: And now, since we have learned these things, you do well in writing to us concerning your peace.
verses.12:23: Moreover, we also have written back to you: 'Our livestock and our possessions are yours, and yours are ours.' Therefore we have commanded that these things be reported to you."
verses.12:24: And Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had returned with a great army, more than before, to fight against him.
verses.12:25: And he went out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Hamath, for he had not given them opportunity to enter his region.
verses.12:26: And he sent spies into their camp, and when they returned, they reported that they were planning to come upon them by night.
verses.12:27: Now when the sun had set, Jonathan commanded his men to keep watch and to be under arms, ready for battle all night, and he stationed guards all around the camp.
verses.12:28: And the adversaries heard that Jonathan with his men was ready for war, and they feared and were terrified in their heart, and they lit fires in their camp.
verses.12:29: But Jonathan and those who were with him did not know until morning, and they saw the lights burning.
verses.12:30: And Jonathan pursued them, and he did not overtake them, for they had crossed the Eleutherus River.
verses.12:31: And Jonathan turned aside against the Arabs who are called Zabadeans, and he struck them and took their spoils.
verses.12:32: And he broke camp and came to Damascus, and he traveled through all that region.
verses.12:33: Now Simon went out and came as far as Ashkelon and to the nearby fortresses, and he turned aside to Joppa and occupied it
verses.12:34: (for he had heard that they wished to hand over the fortress to the party of Demetrius), and he stationed guards there to guard it.
verses.12:35: And Jonathan returned and called together the elders of the people, and he planned with them to build fortresses in Judea,
verses.12:36: and to build walls in Jerusalem, and to raise a great height between the citadel and the city, so that he might separate it from the city, so that it might be by itself, and so that they might neither buy nor sell.
verses.12:37: And they gathered together to build the city; and the wall that was above the brook on the east collapsed, and he repaired it, the one that is called Caphetetha.
verses.12:38: And Simon built Adiada in the Shephelah, and fortified it, and set up gates and bars.
verses.12:39: And when Trypho had planned to reign over Asia, and to take up the diadem, and to stretch out his hand against King Antiochus,
verses.12:40: fearing that perhaps Jonathan would not permit him, but would fight against him, he sought to seize him and kill him. And rising up, he went to Beth-shan.
verses.12:41: And Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand chosen men for battle, and he came to Beth-shan.
verses.12:42: And Trypho saw that Jonathan had come with a great army to stretch out his hands against him; he was afraid,
verses.12:43: and he received him with honor, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts; and he commanded his armies to obey him just as himself.
verses.12:44: And he said to Jonathan, "Why have you troubled the entire people when we have no war?
verses.12:45: And now send them back to their homes, but choose for yourself a few men to be with you, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I will hand it over to you, and the remaining fortresses, and the army, and all those in charge of affairs; and I will turn back and depart, for this is why I came."
verses.12:46: And he trusted him and did as he said; and he dismissed the army, and they went away into the land of Judah.
verses.12:47: However, he kept three thousand men with himself, of whom he sent back two thousand into Galilee, while one thousand came with him.
verses.12:48: Now when Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates of the city and seized him, and all who had entered with him they killed with the sword.
verses.12:49: And Trypho sent an army and horsemen into Galilee and into the great plain to destroy all the companions of Jonathan.
verses.12:50: But when they learned that Jonathan had been seized and had perished, and all who were with him, they encouraged one another and went out ready for battle.
verses.12:51: And those who had pursued them, seeing that it was a matter of life for them, turned back;
verses.12:52: but they all came in peace into the land of Judah. And they lamented Jonathan and those who had been with him greatly, and Israel mourned with great mourning.
verses.12:53: And all the nations that were around them sought to crush them, for they said, "They have no leader and helper; now therefore let us fight against them and remove their memory from among men."
verses.13:1: And Simon heard that Trypho had gathered a large army to come into the land of Judah and devastate it.
verses.13:2: Seeing that the people were in trembling and in fear, he went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people.
verses.13:3: And encouraging them, he said, "You know what great things I and my brothers and my father's house have done for the laws and for the holy places, what battles and distresses we have seen.
verses.13:4: For the sake of these things all my brothers have perished on account of Israel, and I alone am left.
verses.13:5: And now may it not happen to me to spare my life in any time of tribulation, for I am not better than my brothers.
verses.13:6: Therefore I will avenge my nation and the holy places, and our children and wives as well, because all the nations have gathered together to crush us out of hostility."
verses.13:7: And the spirit of the people was kindled as soon as they heard these words.
verses.13:8: And they answered with a loud voice, saying, "You are our commander in place of Judas and your brother Jonathan.
verses.13:9: Fight our battle, and everything that you tell us we will do."
verses.13:10: And gathering all the fighting men, he hastened to complete all the walls of Jerusalem, and he fortified it all around.
verses.13:11: And he sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a new army, to Joppa; and having driven out those who were in it, he himself remained there.
verses.13:12: And Trypho set out from Ptolemais with a great army to come into the land of Judah, and Jonathan was with him under guard.
verses.13:13: But Simon encamped at Addus, facing the plain.
verses.13:14: And when Trypho learned that Simon had risen up in place of his brother Jonathan, and that he was about to engage in battle with him, he sent envoys to him,
verses.13:15: saying, "On account of the silver that your brother Jonathan owed to the king's account because of the affairs that he had, we have detained him.
verses.13:16: And now send one hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that when released he will not flee from us, and we will send him back."
verses.13:17: And Simon knew that he was speaking to him with deceit; yet he ordered the silver and the boys to be given, so that he would not incur great hostility from the people of Israel, who would say,
verses.13:18: "Because he did not send him the silver and the boys, for that reason he perished."
verses.13:19: And he sent the boys and one hundred talents; and he lied, and did not release Jonathan.
verses.13:20: And after these things Trypho came into the region to crush it; and they circled around by the road that leads to Ador, and Simon and his camp marched to every place wherever they went.
verses.13:21: Now those who were in the citadel sent envoys to Trypho, that he should hurry to come through the wilderness and send them provisions.
verses.13:22: And Trypho prepared all the cavalry to come that night; but there was very much snow, and he did not come into Gilead.
verses.13:23: And when he had approached Bascama, he killed Jonathan and his sons there.
verses.13:24: And Trypho turned back and departed to his own land.
verses.13:25: And Simon sent and took the bones of his brother Jonathan, and buried them in Modin, the city of his fathers.
verses.13:26: And all Israel lamented him with a great lamentation, and mourned him for many days.
verses.13:27: And Simon built over the tomb of his father and his brothers a structure high to the sight, with polished stone behind and in front.
verses.13:28: And he set up seven pyramids, one opposite another, for his father and mother and four brothers.
verses.13:29: And around these he placed great columns, and upon the columns armor for an eternal memorial, and beside the armor carved ships, so that they might be seen by all who sail the sea.
verses.13:30: This is the tomb that he made in Modin, to this day.
verses.13:31: Now Trypho, while traveling with the young king Antiochus, killed him by deceit.
verses.13:32: And he reigned in his place, and placed upon himself the diadem of Asia, and caused a great calamity in the land.
verses.13:33: And Simon built the strongholds of Judea, fortifying them with high towers and great walls and gates and bars, and he placed provisions in the fortifications.
verses.13:34: And Simon chose men and sent them to King Demetrius, that he might grant remission to the region, because all the deeds of Trypho had been carried out through plunder.
verses.13:35: And King Demetrius answered him concerning these words, and wrote a letter as follows:
verses.13:36: "King Demetrius to Simon, the high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and the nation of the Jews: greetings.
verses.13:37: We have received the golden crown and the palm branch that you sent, and we are ready to make a great peace with you and to write to the king's officials to remit to you what we have granted.
verses.13:38: For whatever we have decreed stands firm for you; let the fortifications that you have built be yours.
verses.13:39: We also remit the oversights and sins up to this present day, and the crown that you owed; and if anything else was subject to tribute in Jerusalem, let it no longer be subject to tribute.
verses.13:40: And if any of you are fit to be enrolled among our men, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us."
verses.13:41: In the one hundred and seventieth year, the yoke of the nations was taken away from Israel.
verses.13:42: And the people of Israel began to write on documents and public records, "In the first year under Simon, the high priest, great commander, and prince of the Jews."
verses.13:43: In those days Simon encamped against Gaza and surrounded it with a camp; and he made siege engines and brought them up to the city, and he struck one tower and captured it.
verses.13:44: And those who were inside the siege engine burst out into the city, and a great commotion arose in the city.
verses.13:45: And those who were in the city went up with their wives and children upon the wall, with their tunics torn, and cried out with a loud voice, asking Simon that right hands be given to them,
verses.13:46: and they said, "Do not repay us according to our evil deeds, but according to your mercies."
verses.13:47: And Simon, being moved, did not make war against them; yet he drove them out of the city, and cleansed the houses in which the idols had been, and then he entered into it with hymns, blessing the Lord.
verses.13:48: And having cast out all uncleanness from it, he settled in it men who would practice the law; and he fortified it, and made a dwelling for himself.
verses.13:49: Now those who were in the citadel of Jerusalem were prevented from going out and entering the region, and from buying and selling; and they became very hungry, and many of them perished from hunger.
verses.13:50: And they cried out to Simon that they might receive right hands, and he gave them to them; and he drove them out from there, and cleansed the citadel from defilements.
verses.13:51: And they entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise, and palm branches, and lyres, and cymbals, and harps, and hymns, and songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
verses.13:52: And he decreed that every year these days should be observed with gladness.
verses.13:53: And Simon saw his son John, that he was a valiant man of battle, and he appointed him commander of all the forces; and he lived in Gazara.
verses.14:1: In the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his army and departed into Media to assemble auxiliary forces for himself, so that he might defeat Trypho.
verses.14:2: And Arsaces, king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had entered his borders, and he sent one of his commanders to capture him alive and bring him to himself.
verses.14:3: And he departed and struck the camp of Demetrius, and captured him, and led him to Arsaces, and placed him in custody.
verses.14:4: And the whole land of Judah was quiet all the days of Simon, and he sought good things for his nation, and his authority and his glory pleased them all the days.
verses.14:5: And with all his glory, he took Joppa as a harbor and made an entrance to the islands of the sea.
verses.14:6: And he extended the borders of his nation and gained control of the region.
verses.14:7: And he gathered many captives, and he ruled over Gazara, Beth-zur, and the citadel; and he removed the impurities from it, and there was no one who resisted him.
verses.14:8: And each one cultivated his own land in peace; and the land of Judah yielded its fruits, and the trees of the fields their fruit.
verses.14:9: All the elders sat in the public squares and discussed the good things of the land, and the young men clothed themselves with glory and robes of war.
verses.14:10: And he supplied provisions to the cities and established them to be instruments of fortification, until the name of his glory was named to the end of the earth.
verses.14:11: He made peace over the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy.
verses.14:12: And each one sat under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and there was no one who frightened them.
verses.14:13: There ceased to be anyone fighting against them upon the land; kings were crushed in those days.
verses.14:14: And he strengthened all the humble of his people, and he sought out the law and removed every unjust and evil person.
verses.14:15: He glorified the sanctuary and multiplied the vessels of the sanctuary.
verses.14:16: And it was heard in Rome that Jonathan had died, and even as far as the Spartans, and they were deeply grieved.
verses.14:17: But when they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place, and that he himself held control of the whole region and the cities in it,
verses.14:18: they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew the friendship and the alliance which they had made with Judas and with Jonathan, his brothers.
verses.14:19: And they were read in the presence of the assembly in Jerusalem. And this is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent:
verses.14:20: "The rulers and cities of the Spartans, to Simon the great priest, and to the elders, and to the priests, and to the rest of the people of the Jews, brothers: greetings.
verses.14:21: The envoys who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory, honor, and joy, and we rejoiced at their arrival.
verses.14:22: And we wrote down what had been spoken by them in the councils of the people, as follows: 'Numenius, son of Antiochus, and Antipater, son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us, renewing the former friendship with us.
verses.14:23: And it pleased the people to receive the men gloriously and to place a copy of their words in the reserved books of the people, so that it may be for a memorial to the people of the Spartans.' And we have written a copy of these things to Simon the great priest."
verses.14:24: After these things, Simon sent Numenius to Rome, carrying a great golden shield weighing one thousand minas, to establish an alliance with them. Now when the Roman people heard
verses.14:25: these words, they said, "What thanksgiving shall we return to Simon and his sons?
verses.14:26: For he himself restored his brothers and fought off the enemies of Israel from them." And they established freedom for him, and inscribed it on bronze tablets, and placed them on pillars on Mount Zion.
verses.14:27: And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth day of the month of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, in the third year under Simon the great priest in Asaramel,
verses.14:28: in a great assembly of the priests, and of the people, and of the rulers of the nation, and of the elders of the region, these things were made known: since battles frequently took place in our region,
verses.14:29: Simon, son of Mattathias, of the sons of Jarib, and his brothers gave themselves to danger and resisted the adversaries of their nation, so that their sanctuary and the law might stand, and with great glory they glorified their nation.
verses.14:30: And Jonathan gathered his nation, and became great priest for them, and was joined to his people.
verses.14:31: And their enemies wanted to trample and crush their region and to stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.
verses.14:32: Then Simon resisted and fought for his nation, and spent large sums of money, and armed the men of valor of his nation, and gave them wages;
verses.14:33: and he fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth-zur, which was on the borders of Judea, where the weapons of the enemies were previously, and he placed a garrison of Jewish men there.
verses.14:34: And he fortified Joppa, which was by the sea, and Gazara, which is on the borders of Azotus, in which enemies previously lived; and he settled Jews there, and whatever things were suitable for their correction he placed in them.
verses.14:35: And the people saw the conduct of Simon and the glory which he planned to do for his nation, and they appointed him their leader and chief priest, because he himself had done all these things, and for the justice and faithfulness which he preserved for his nation, and he sought in every way to exalt his people.
verses.14:36: And in his days it prospered in his hands, so that the Gentiles were removed from their region, and those who were in the city of David, in Jerusalem, in the citadel, from which they would come out and defile all the things that are around the sanctuary and inflict a great blow upon purity;
verses.14:37: and he stationed Jewish men in it for the protection of the region and of the city, and he heightened the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.14:38: And King Demetrius established the high priesthood for him.
verses.14:39: In accordance with these things, he made him his friend and glorified him with great glory.
verses.14:40: For he heard that the Jews had been called friends, allies, and brothers by the Romans, and that they had received the envoys of Simon gloriously,
verses.14:41: and that the Jews and their priests had consented that he should be their leader and high priest forever, until a faithful prophet should arise;
verses.14:42: and that he should be leader over them, and that he should have care for the sanctuary, and that he should appoint overseers over their works, and over the region, and over the weapons, and over the garrisons;
verses.14:43: and that he should have care concerning the sanctuary; and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all documents in the region should be written in his name; and that he should be clothed in purple and gold;
verses.14:44: and that it should not be lawful for anyone of the people or of the priests to nullify any of these things, or to contradict the things spoken by him, or to convene an assembly in the region without him, or to dress in purple, or to wear a golden clasp.
verses.14:45: And whoever acts contrary to these things, or nullifies any of these things, will be guilty."
verses.14:46: And it pleased all the people to appoint Simon and to act according to these words.
verses.14:47: And Simon accepted, and it pleased him to exercise the high priesthood, and to be leader and ruler of the nation of the Jews and of the priests, and to preside over all.
verses.14:48: And they ordered this writing to be placed on bronze tablets, and for them to be placed in the enclosure of the sanctuary, in a prominent place;
verses.14:49: and a copy of them to be placed in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have it.
verses.15:1: And King Antiochus, the son of Demetrius, sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and ruler of the nation of the Jews, and to the whole nation;
verses.15:2: and they contained this wording: "King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.15:3: Since indeed pestilent men have taken possession of the kingdom of our fathers, I intend to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before; and I have formed a chosen multitude of an army, and I have built warships.
verses.15:4: Now I intend to advance through the country so that I may take vengeance on those who have ruined our country and who have laid waste many cities in my kingdom.
verses.15:5: Now therefore I establish for you all the offerings which all the kings before me remitted to you, and whatever other gifts they remitted to you;
verses.15:6: and I permit you to strike your own coinage in your country;
verses.15:7: and let Jerusalem be holy and free; and all the weapons that have been made, and the fortresses that you have built, which you hold, let them remain yours.
verses.15:8: And every debt owed to the king, and whatever will be owed to the king in the future, from this time and for all time, are remitted to you.
verses.15:9: And when we have gained possession of our kingdom, we will glorify you, and your nation, and the temple, with great glory, so that your glory may be made known in all the earth."
verses.15:10: In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year, Antiochus went out into the land of his fathers, and all the armies came together to him, so that few were left with Trypho.
verses.15:11: And King Antiochus pursued him, and he came to Dora, fleeing along the seacoast;
verses.15:12: for he knew that evils had gathered against him, and that the army had abandoned him.
verses.15:13: And Antiochus encamped against Dora with one hundred and twenty thousand fighting men and eight thousand horsemen;
verses.15:14: and he surrounded the city, and the ships approached from the sea; and they harassed the city by land and sea, and allowed no one to go in or go out.
verses.15:15: Now Numenius, and those who had been with him, came from the city of Rome, carrying letters written to the kings and countries, in which these things were contained:
verses.15:16: "Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
verses.15:17: Envoys of the Jews, our friends, have come to us, renewing the former friendship and alliance, sent by Simon the chief priest and the people of the Jews.
verses.15:18: Moreover, they also brought a golden shield of one thousand minas.
verses.15:19: Therefore it has seemed good to us to write to the kings and countries, that they should not bring evils upon them, nor fight against them, their cities, or their countries, and that they should not give aid to those fighting against them.
verses.15:20: It has also seemed right to us to accept the shield from them.
verses.15:21: If therefore any pestilent men have fled from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the chief priest, so that he may punish them according to his law."
verses.15:22: These same things were written to King Demetrius, and to Attalus, and to Ariarathes, and to Arsaces,
verses.15:23: and to all the countries: to Lampsacus, and to the Spartans, and to Delos, and to Myndus, and to Sicyon, and to Caria, and to Samos, and to Pamphylia, and to Lycia, and to Halicarnassus, and to Cos, and to Side, and to Aradus, and to Rhodes, and to Phaselis, and to Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
verses.15:24: And they wrote a copy of them to Simon the chief priest and to the people of the Jews.
verses.15:25: Meanwhile King Antiochus pitched camp against Dora a second time, continually bringing forces against it and building siege engines; and he shut Trypho in so that he could not go out.
verses.15:26: And Simon sent to him two thousand chosen men for aid, and silver, and gold, and abundant equipment.
verses.15:27: And he refused to accept them, but broke everything that he had agreed to with him before, and alienated himself from him.
verses.15:28: And he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to confer with him, saying, "You hold Joppa, and Gazara, and the citadel that is in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom;
verses.15:29: you have laid waste their territories, and inflicted a great blow in the land, and exercised dominion throughout many places in my kingdom.
verses.15:30: Now therefore hand over the cities that you have seized, and the tributes of the places over which you have exercised dominion outside the borders of Judea;
verses.15:31: but if not, give for them five hundred talents of silver, and for the destruction that you have caused and for the tributes of the cities, another five hundred talents; otherwise, we will come and wage war against you."
verses.15:32: And Athenobius, the friend of the king, came to Jerusalem, and saw the glory of Simon, and the splendor in gold and silver, and the abundant array; and he was astounded, and reported to him the words of the king.
verses.15:33: And Simon answered him and said to him, "We have neither taken another's land nor do we hold what belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers, which was unjustly possessed by our enemies for a time.
verses.15:34: We, however, having the opportunity, are reclaiming the inheritance of our fathers.
verses.15:35: For as for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand, they themselves were inflicting a great blow among the people and in our country; for these we give one hundred talents." And Athenobius did not answer him a word.
verses.15:36: Returning in anger to the king, he reported to him these words, and the glory of Simon, and everything that he had seen; and the king became angry with great anger.
verses.15:37: Meanwhile Trypho fled by ship to Orthosia.
verses.15:38: And the king appointed Cendebeus commander of the seacoast, and gave him an army of foot soldiers and horsemen.
verses.15:39: And he commanded him to move camp facing Judea, and he commanded him to build Gedor, and to barricade the gates of the city, and to make war on the people. Meanwhile the king was pursuing Trypho.
verses.15:40: And Cendebeus arrived at Jamnia, and began to provoke the populace, and to trample Judea, and to take the people captive and kill them, and to build Gedor.
verses.15:41: And he stationed horsemen and an army there, so that going out they might traverse the road of Judea, just as the king had directed him.
verses.16:1: And John went up from Gazara and reported to his father Simon what Cendebeus had done among their people.
verses.16:2: And Simon called his two older sons, Judas and John, and said to them, "I, and my brothers, and the house of my father have waged war against the enemies of Israel from youth until this day; and it has prospered in our hands to deliver Israel several times.
verses.16:3: Now, however, I have grown old; instead, stand in place of me and my brothers, and go out and fight for our nation; and may help from heaven be with you."
verses.16:4: And he chose from the country twenty thousand fighting men and horsemen; and they set out against Cendebeus, and slept in Modin.
verses.16:5: And they rose in the morning and went into the plain; and look, a numerous army of foot soldiers and horsemen was coming to meet them, and a torrent stream was between them.
verses.16:6: And he and his people moved camp facing them, and he saw the people afraid to cross the torrent; and he crossed over first, and the men saw him and crossed after him.
verses.16:7: And he divided the people, with the horsemen in the middle of the foot soldiers; now the cavalry of the adversaries was exceedingly numerous.
verses.16:8: And they sounded out with the sacred trumpets, and Cendebeus and his camp were turned to flight; and many of them fell wounded, while the rest fled into the stronghold.
verses.16:9: Then Judas, the brother of John, was wounded; but John pursued them until he came to Kedron, which he had built;
verses.16:10: and they fled as far as the towers that were in the fields of Azotus, and he burned them with fire. And two thousand men of them fell, and he returned to Judea in peace.
verses.16:11: And Ptolemy, the son of Abubus, had been appointed commander in the plain of Jericho, and he had much silver and gold;
verses.16:12: for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.
verses.16:13: And his heart was lifted up, and he wanted to gain possession of the country, and he plotted treachery against Simon and his sons, so that he might do away with them.
verses.16:14: Now Simon, traveling through the cities that were in the country of Judea and taking care of them, went down to Jericho, he himself, and his son Mattathias, and Judas, in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month; this is the month of Shebat.
verses.16:15: And the son of Abubus received them with treachery into the small stronghold called Dok, which he had built; and he made a great banquet for them, and hid men there.
verses.16:16: And when Simon and his sons had become drunk, Ptolemy rose up with his men, and they took their weapons and entered the banquet; and they killed him, and his two sons, and some of his servants;
verses.16:17: and he committed great deception in Israel, and repaid evil for good.
verses.16:18: And Ptolemy wrote these things and sent to the king, that he might send him an army for aid, and he would hand over to him the country, and their cities, and the tributes.
verses.16:19: And he sent others to Gazara to do away with John; and to the tribunes he sent letters, that they should come to him, and he would give them silver, and gold, and gifts.
verses.16:20: And he sent others to seize Jerusalem and the mountain of the temple.
verses.16:21: And someone running ahead reported to John in Gazara that his father and his brothers had perished, and, "He has sent for you also to be killed."
verses.16:22: Now when he heard this, he was greatly terrified; and he seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them, for he knew that they were seeking to destroy him.
verses.16:23: And the rest of the accounts of John, and of his wars, and of the noble deeds of valor in which he acted bravely, and of the building of the walls that he constructed, and of his deeds,
verses.16:24: look, these are written in the book of the days of his priesthood, from the time he was made high priest after his father.

notes.1:4: The Vulgate places the lifting up of Alexander's heart at the end of verse 4 (with both passive verbs agreeing with 'his heart') and omits the Greek clause stating that he ruled over countries, nations, and rulers who became tributary to him.
notes.1:10: Latin 'illustris' ('the Illustrious') translates the Greek royal epithet 'Epiphanes' ('Manifest' or 'Illustrious') of Antiochus IV.
notes.1:16: The Vulgate reads 'cœpit regnare' ('he began to reign'), whereas the Greek reads that he intended or conceived the plan to reign.
notes.1:22: In the Clementine Vulgate, this clause stands after the plundering of the sanctuary in verse 21 (where Latin 'comminuit' also reads 'shattered' rather than the Greek 'stripped off'), whereas in the Greek it appears at the end of verse 20.
notes.1:30: The Clementine Vulgate omits the latter part of verse 30 found in the Greek, which recounts the sudden assault on the city and the destruction of many people of Israel.
notes.1:36: Latin 'diabolum malum' (literally 'an evil devil' or 'adversary') follows the Greek loanword 'diabolon' (representing Hebrew 'satan', adversary); the Vulgate also omits 'continually' at the end of the verse.
notes.1:44: The Vulgate reads 'leges gentium terræ' ('the laws of the nations of the land'), whereas the Greek reads 'customs foreign to the land.'
notes.1:45: Latin 'placationes' ('propitiations') differs from the Greek 'sponden' ('drink offering'), and in verse 46 the Vulgate omits the Greek clause about profaning Sabbaths and feasts.
notes.1:48: In the Clementine Vulgate, the clause numbered as verse 49 in the Greek ('so that they would forget the law and alter all the ordinances of God') is joined to the end of verse 48, so verse 49 is omitted in numbering.
notes.1:59: Latin distinguishes 'ara' (a pagan altar) from 'altare' (the temple altar of God), and the Vulgate reads 'contra' ('opposite') rather than the Greek 'upon.'
notes.2:1: The Vulgate adds "Mount" (in monte Modin), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads simply "in Modein."
notes.2:9: The Vulgate reads "her old men" (senes ejus), whereas the Greek Septuagint has "her infants" (nepia).
notes.2:21: Literally "May God be gracious to us" (propitius sit nobis Deus), a biblical oath idiom equivalent to "Far be it from us."
notes.2:26: The Vulgate reads "Salomi" (matching Greek "Salom"), whereas Hebrew Numbers 25:14 calls Zimri's father "Salu."
notes.2:31: The Vulgate places "and that many had gone after them" within the report to the king's men as indirect speech, whereas the Greek Septuagint begins verse 32 with "many pursued them," referring to the king's forces.
notes.2:48: "Give a horn" (dederant cornu) is a biblical idiom meaning to yield power, strength, or victory.
notes.2:54: The Vulgate specifies "the zeal of God" (zelum Dei), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads simply "being zealous with zeal."
notes.2:55: The Latin uses "Jesus" (the Greek/Latin form of "Joshua") and calls him a "leader" (dux), whereas the Greek Septuagint calls him a "judge" (krites).
notes.2:63: The Vulgate reads "his earth" (terram suam), whereas the Greek Septuagint has "his dust" (choun autou).
notes.3:3: The Vulgate reads "in battles" (in præliis) rather than the Greek verb phrase ("he set battles in array"), and adds "his" to "sword" (gladio suo).
notes.3:6: Latin directa est (lit. "was directed" or "was guided straight") is an idiom expressing success or prosperity.
notes.3:13: The Vulgate attaches "of the faithful" to "congregation" (congregationem fidelium, et ecclesiam secum) and omits the closing clause found in the Greek ("and of those going out to war").
notes.3:18: The Vulgate explicitly reads "the God of heaven" (Dei cæli) here and "the Lord Himself" (ipse Dominus) in 3:22, where the standard Greek text uses only "Heaven" and "He" respectively.
notes.3:41: Vulgate "servants" (pueros, also meaning "boys") reflects a reading of Greek paidas ("servants/boys") rather than pedas ("fetters/chains") found in standard Greek manuscripts; likewise "of the foreigners" (alienigenarum) replaces the Greek "of the Philistines."
notes.3:48: This clause is grammatically difficult in both Latin and Greek, referring either to the matters about which the nations consulted the images of their idols (contrasting with Israel consulting the law) or to the nations searching the books of the law to paint idol images in them.
notes.3:53: The Vulgate explicitly adds "God" (Deus), whereas the standard Greek text reads simply "unless you help us."
notes.3:55: The Vulgate uses Roman military titles (tribunos, centuriones, decuriones) alongside the Greek loanword pentacontarchos ("commanders of fifty") for commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
notes.4:6: The Vulgate adds "only" ("only three thousand men") and omits the Greek qualifier "as they wished," stating unconditionally that Judas's men lacked armor and swords.
notes.4:10: The Vulgate reads the confident statement "and the Lord will have mercy on us," whereas Greek manuscripts have a conditional clause ("if he favors us") without explicitly naming the Lord.
notes.4:16: The Vulgate reads "and his army was following him" (et exercitus ejus sequens eum), whereas Greek manuscripts say that Judas and his force returned "from pursuing after them."
notes.4:29: The Vulgate reads "Judea" and "Beth-horon," whereas Greek manuscripts read "Idumea" and "Beth-zur."
notes.4:44: The Vulgate uses singular verbs ("he deliberated ... what he should do"), referring to Judas, whereas Greek manuscripts use the plural ("they deliberated ... what they should do").
notes.4:48: The Vulgate reads "both the shrine and the courts" (et ædem, et atria), whereas Greek manuscripts mention sanctifying only the courts.
notes.4:61: The Vulgate reads "and he fortified it to watch over Beth-zur" (et munivit eum ad custodiendum Bethsuram), whereas Greek manuscripts say that they fortified Beth-zur itself to guard it.
notes.5:8: The Vulgate reads "Gazer" (a name elsewhere associated with Gezer in Judea), whereas the Greek reads "Jazer" (a Transjordanian city in Ammonite territory). "Its daughters" is a biblical idiom for dependent surrounding villages and towns.
notes.5:13: The Vulgate reads "in the districts of Tubin" (in locis Tubin), corresponding to the territory of Tob (Greek Toubiou) east of the Jordan.
notes.5:15: The Vulgate renders this clause as a distinct passive statement, "all Galilee has been filled with foreigners" (repleta est omnis Galilaea alienigenis), whereas the Greek lists "all Galilee of the Gentiles" among the attacking regions. The Latin also shifts abruptly from indirect speech ("against them") to direct speech ("us").
notes.5:26: The Vulgate preserves the place-name forms "Barasa," "Casphor," and "Mageth," where the Greek text commonly reads "Bosora" (Bozrah), "Chaspho," and "Maked."
notes.5:31: The Vulgate reads "the cry of battle rose up to heaven like a trumpet, and a great cry from the city," whereas the Greek reads "the cry of the city went up to heaven with trumpets and a great shout."
notes.5:36: The Vulgate reads "Casbon" for the city called "Casphor" in 5:26, where the Greek reads "Chasphon" or "Chaspho."
notes.5:42: The Vulgate reads "Leave no man behind" (Neminem hominem reliqueritis), whereas the Greek reads "Do not allow any man to encamp."
notes.5:45: The Vulgate reads "and a very great army" (et exercitum magnum valde), omitting the Greek mention of their "baggage" and rendering the Greek appositional phrase ("a very great company") as a coordinated noun phrase.
notes.5:63: The Vulgate reads "the men of Judah" (viri Juda), whereas the Greek reads "the man Judas and his brothers."
notes.5:66: The Vulgate reads "Samaria" (reflecting a major Greek manuscript tradition), whereas some other Greek witnesses read "Marissa" (Mareshah), which lies directly between Hebron and Azotus.
notes.6:7: Latin civitatem suam uses the reflexive possessive, which grammatically refers to the plural subject ("their city," that is, the Jews'), whereas the Greek reads singular "his city" (referring to King Antiochus).
notes.6:12: Vulgate reads omnia spolia aurea et argentea ("all the golden and silver spoils"), whereas the Greek has "all the vessels of silver and gold."
notes.6:18: Latin quærebant eis mala semper, et firmamentum gentium literally pairs "evils for them" and "a support [or stronghold] of the Gentiles" as objects of "were seeking," mirroring the concise syntax of the Greek.
notes.6:25: Vulgate reads in omnes fines nostros ("against all our borders"), whereas the Greek reads "against all their borders."
notes.6:26: Vulgate reads munitionem Bethsuram munierunt ("they have fortified the fortress of Beth-zur"), whereas the Greek reads "they have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur."
notes.6:37: Vulgate reads et super eas machinæ ("and upon them were engines"), whereas the Greek describes the wooden towers as fastened onto each beast with contrivances.
notes.6:38: Vulgate reads tubis exercitum commovere, et perurgere constipatos in legionibus ejus ("to rouse the army with trumpets and to press forward those packed closely together in his legions"), differing notably from the Greek, which speaks of shielding the army and being armored in his phalanxes.
notes.6:41: Vulgate reads omnes inhabitantes terram ("all the inhabitants of the land"), whereas the Greek reads "all who heard."
notes.6:43: Vulgate reads Eleazar filius Saura ("Eleazar, son of Saura"), a Vulgate-distinct name reflecting a Greek textual variant where the standard Greek reads "Eleazar called Avaran."
notes.6:53: Vulgate reads in civitate ("in the city") and qui remanserant ("those who had remained"), whereas the Greek reads "in the storage vessels" and "those who had been brought to safety."
notes.7:8: The Vulgate construes magnum ("great") with "the river" (trans flumen magnum in regno), whereas the Greek applies "great" to Bacchides ("great in the kingdom"); in 7:9 the Vulgate also adds "so that he might see the destruction that Judas had done."
notes.7:19: The Vulgate preserves the distinctive place name Bethzecha (Greek: Beth-zaith/Bezeth) and reads qui a se effugerant ("who had fled from him"), whereas the Greek reads "who had deserted to him."
notes.7:32: The Vulgate reads quinque millia ("five thousand"), whereas Greek manuscripts read "five hundred."
notes.7:40: The Vulgate gives the distinctive place-name spellings Adarsa here and Adazer in 7:45 (both corresponding to Greek Adasa); in 7:41 it also explicitly names King Sennacherib and reads angelus ("an angel") rather than "the king" and "your angel."
notes.7:46: The Vulgate reads ventilabant eos cornibus ("tossed them with horns," an idiom akin to Ps 43:6), rendering literally the Greek military verb for "outflanked them."
notes.8:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads acquiescunt ad omnia quae postulantur ab eis ("consent to all things that are requested of them"), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads "they are favorably disposed to all who approach them."
notes.8:2: The Vulgate reads Et audierunt ("And they heard"), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads "And they told him."
notes.8:8: The Vulgate uses plural ethnic terms ("the region of the Indians, and the Medes, and the Lydians") and plural ab eis ("from them", vs. Greek "from him"), preserving the Septuagint tradition of India, Media, and Lydia (historically associated with Ionia, Mysia, and Lydia).
notes.8:15: The Clementine Vulgate puts trecentos viginti in the accusative case as the object of consulebant ("they consulted three hundred twenty men"), whereas the Greek Septuagint uses the nominative ("three hundred twenty took counsel").
notes.8:17: The Vulgate reads filii Jacob ("the son of Jacob"), a Vulgate-distinct proper name where the Greek Septuagint reads Akkos (Hakkoz).
notes.9:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads Laisa, whereas most Greek manuscripts read Elasa.
notes.9:24: The Vulgate distinctly adds "to Bacchides" (Bacchidi) and "their whole" (omnis ... eorum), whereas the Greek reads simply that "the country defected with them."
notes.9:35: Latin commodarent means "lend"; the Greek has Jonathan's party asking to leave its abundant baggage with the Nabateans.
notes.9:37: The Vulgate reads "from Medeba" (ex Madaba), where the Greek reads "from Nadabath." Latin ambitione here carries its late-Latin sense of "pomp" or "stately display" (Greek: "a great escort").
notes.9:45: The Vulgate reads only "in front of us" (ex adverso, without the Greek "and behind us") and adds "the banks" (ripæ) before the marshes and thickets.
notes.9:48: The Vulgate compresses the longer Greek text ("and swam across to the other side, and the enemy did not cross the Jordan against them") into "and they swam across the Jordan to them."
notes.9:50: The Vulgate preserves the distinct place-name forms Phara (Greek: Pharathon) and Thopo (Greek: Tephon).
notes.9:62: The Vulgate reads Bethbessen (so also in 9:64), whereas most Greek manuscripts read Bethbasi.
notes.9:66: The Vulgate reads the name Odaren (Greek: Odomera) and "to grow in forces" (crescere in virtutibus), where the Greek has "to go up with forces."
notes.10:1: The Vulgate renders the Greek royal epithet Epiphanes as Nobilis ("the Noble").
notes.10:5: The Vulgate has singular fratrem ejus ("his brother"), whereas the Greek text reads plural ("his brothers").
notes.10:31: The Vulgate reads et decimæ et tributa ipsius sint ("and let the tithes and tributes be its own"), assigning those revenues to Jerusalem itself rather than phrasing them as exemptions as in the Greek.
notes.10:36: The Vulgate reads in munitionibus regis magni ("in the fortresses of the great king"), construing magni with "king" rather than with "fortresses" ("the great fortresses of the king") as in the Greek.
notes.10:39: The Vulgate renders the Greek phrase for "the sanctuary" with masculine sanctis qui sunt ("the holy ones who are"), while sanctorum at the end of the verse and in vv. 42 and 44 refers to the sanctuary.
notes.10:49: The Vulgate reads fugit exercitus Demetrii, et insecutus est eum Alexander ("the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued him"), reversing the Greek text, in which Alexander's army flees and Demetrius pursues.
notes.10:68: The Clementine Vulgate uses the masculine accusative form Antiochum (without a preposition, as a city of destination) in place of Antiochiam ("to Antioch").
notes.10:71: The Vulgate reads virtus bellorum ("the power of wars"), whereas the Greek text has "the power of the cities."
notes.10:79: The Vulgate adds in castris ("in the camp"), a detail absent from the Greek text.
notes.10:83: The Vulgate renders the Greek "their idol-temple" literally as idolum suum ("their idol"), and omits the Greek subject "the cavalry" before qui dispersi sunt ("those who were scattered").
notes.11:4: The Clementine Vulgate renders the surroundings of Azotus broadly as cetera ejus ("the rest of it") and reads tumulos ("burial mounds") of those killed in the war, whereas the Greek refers to its surrounding towns and to heaps of burned bodies piled along the road.
notes.11:18: Latin perierunt ab his qui erant intra castra literally means "perished by those who were inside the camps," distinguishing castra ("camps") from munitionibus ("strongholds") where the Greek repeats "in the strongholds."
notes.11:28: The Clementine Vulgate coordinates Samaria and its bordering territories alongside the three districts (Latin toparchias), whereas most Greek witnesses read "the three districts of Samaria."
notes.11:34: The Clementine Vulgate mentions "three cities" while naming only Lydda and Ramathan (Greek Rathamin) because the third Greek place name, Aphairema, was translated into Latin as the verb sequestrari ("to be set apart").
notes.11:50: Latin dextras (literally "right hands," singular dexteram in 11:62) is an idiom for extending a hand as a pledge of truce or peace.
notes.11:56: Latin bestias ("the beasts") refers to the Seleucid war elephants captured by Trypho.
notes.11:59: The Clementine Vulgate reads a terminis Tyri ("from the borders of Tyre"), whereas the Greek refers to "the Ladder of Tyre," a coastal promontory pass south of Tyre.
notes.11:63: Vulgate prævaricati sunt ("had transgressed") reflects a Greek variant meaning "crossed over/transgressed" rather than the standard Greek reading "had arrived."
notes.11:72: The Clementine Vulgate reads et pugnaverunt ("and they fought"), where the Greek reads "and they fled" (probably an early Latin shift from fugerunt to pugnaverunt).
notes.12:7: The Vulgate reads Arius (also in 12:20), referring to King Areus I of Sparta (Greek Areios, corrupted in some Greek manuscripts).
notes.12:11: Vulgate in observationibus ("in the observances") is a distinct Latin reading where Greek manuscripts read "in prayers" or "in remembrances."
notes.12:32: Latin junxit literally means "he yoked up," an elliptical military expression rendering Greek anazeuxas ("having yoked up [the pack animals]," meaning "breaking camp").
notes.12:37: Caphetetha is the Vulgate-distinct form of the wall name (Greek Chaphenatha); similarly in 12:38 the Vulgate reads Adiada (Greek Adida, Hebrew Hadid).
notes.12:42: The Vulgate construes ut extenderet in eum manus ("to stretch out his hands against him") as the apparent purpose of Jonathan's advance that frightened Trypho, whereas the Greek reads that Trypho "feared to stretch out his hands against him."
notes.13:11: The Vulgate reads exercitum novum ("a new army"), reflecting a Greek variant (kainen, "new") where the Septuagint reads hikanen ("a considerable force").
notes.13:13: The Vulgate proper name Addus corresponds to Adida in the Greek Septuagint.
notes.13:22: The Vulgate omits an intervening Greek clause ("because of the snow, and he departed and came"), yielding the distinct Latin reading that Trypho did not come into Gilead.
notes.13:23: The Vulgate reads occidit Jonathan et filios ejus illic ("killed Jonathan and his sons there"), where the Greek Septuagint reads "killed Jonathan, and he was buried there."
notes.13:37: "The palm branch" translates the Vulgate's rare transliteration bahem (from Greek baine, "palm branch"), paired here with the golden crown.
notes.13:43: The Vulgate names the city Gaza (Gazam), whereas the Greek Septuagint reads Gazara (compare Gazaris, "Gazara," in 13:53).
notes.13:45: "Right hands" literally renders Latin dextras (also in 13:50), an idiom denoting pledges of peace or terms of surrender.
notes.14:24: The Clementine Vulgate explicitly reads populus Romanus ("the Roman people"), making the Romans the speakers in verses 25-26, whereas the Greek text has simply "the people," referring to the Jewish people.
notes.14:26: The Vulgate reads restituit enim ipse fratres suos ("for he himself restored his brothers") and statuerunt ei libertatem ("they established freedom for him"), whereas the Greek has Simon, his brothers, and his father's house standing firm and establishing freedom for Israel.
notes.14:27: Asaramel (Greek Saramel or Asaramel) is a transliterated term commonly understood as deriving from Hebrew hasar am El ("court of the people of God") or denoting an assembly place in Jerusalem.
notes.14:29: The Vulgate reads Jarib here for the priestly family name that appears as Joarib in the Greek text (cf. 1 Maccabees 2:1; 1 Chronicles 24:7).
notes.14:34: The Vulgate reads ad correptionem eorum ("for their correction"), a literal rendering of Greek epanorthosis, which in this context means "restoration," "upkeep," or "provision."
notes.15:3: Vulgate reads "electam ... multitudinem exercitus" ("a chosen multitude of an army"), whereas the Greek refers to mercenary forces.
notes.15:23: Vulgate reads "Lampsaco" ("Lampsacus") where the Greek has Sampsames, and places Cos ahead of Side, Aradus, Rhodes, and Phaselis.
notes.15:32: Vulgate reads "claritatem in auro, et argento" ("the splendor in gold and silver"), where the Greek specifies a sideboard or cupboard of gold and silver vessels.
notes.15:39: Vulgate names the town "Gedorem" ("Gedor") here and in 15:40 (contrast "Cedronem" in 16:9, matching Greek Kedron in all three verses), and reads "obstruere portas civitatis" ("barricade the gates of the city") where the Greek speaks of fortifying the gates.
notes.15:40: Vulgate reads "conculcare Judaeam" ("trample Judea") where the Greek has "invade Judea," and includes "and to build Gedor" at the end of the verse.
notes.16:3: Vulgate reads "loco meo, et fratres mei" (plural "and my brothers," echoing 16:2), whereas the Greek has the singular genitive "and of my brother."
notes.16:8: Vulgate specifies "sacris tubis" ("sacred trumpets"), whereas the Greek simply reads "trumpets."
notes.16:18: Vulgate adds "et tributa" ("and the tributes") to Ptolemy's offer, a phrase absent from the standard Greek text.
notes.16:21: Following the Greek, the Vulgate shifts abruptly from third-person indirect report ("his father and his brothers") to second-person direct address ("you also") after the repeated conjunction "quia."
